sourcing: Sourcing:
- Dhammapada verses use Acharya Buddharakkhita's translation (Buddhist
Publication Society, 1985) unless the entry says otherwise. A few
sutta lines use Thanissaro Bhikkhu's (dhammatalks.org).
- Ajahn Mun and Ajahn Lee are from Thanissaro Bhikkhu's translations on
dhammatalks.org.
- Sayadaw U Tejaniya is from his Tricycle interview "The Wise
Investigator" (Winter 2007) and his book Awareness Alone Is Not Enough.
- Some Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho lines are cross-checked against
Abhayagiri's Ajahn Pasanno Archive, which transcribes from audio.
- Quotes that couldn't be traced to a primary source were left out
rather than carry a vague credit — including several widely-circulated
lines that are almost certainly genuine but unplaceable. Better a
shorter list than one that cites "teachings of X". "Food for the Heart"
and "A Still Forest Pool" are the reliable Ajahn Chah anthologies to
draw more from.
- No Bhikkhu Bodhi Wheel/Bodhi Leaves essay used yet beyond The Noble
Eightfold Path — worth expanding later.
- Japanese Zen entries: Suzuki from Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind (1970) and
Not Always So; Dogen from Moon in a Dewdrop and Fukanzazengi (trans.
Waddell/Abe) and Tenzo Kyokun (trans. Foulk); Hakuin's Song of Zazen
from D.T. Suzuki's Manual of Zen Buddhism translation (wording varies
across translators — this is the most widely cited English version).
A second Hakuin quote (from Wild Ivy) was attempted but the only
candidate line had conflicting, unverifiable phrasing across sources,
so it was left out.
- Sam Harris quotes are both from Waking Up: A Guide to Spirituality
Without Religion (2014), verified against multiple independent
citations of the book's exact text. Could not verify specific
guided-meditation wording from the Waking Up app itself — its audio
sessions aren't publicly transcribed, so nothing from the app proper
was added; see FH for how to proceed on that front.
- Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Sister Chan Khong were researched for this
batch but dropped: every candidate quote traced only to aggregator
sites (Goodreads/AZQuotes) with no accessible primary text to confirm
exact wording. Worth revisiting with direct access to the printed
books (The Heart of Compassion; Learning True Love).
- Ajahn Amaro's Small Boat, Great Mountain quote and Seung Sahn's Only
Don't Know quote were checked against OCR'd scans with some noise
elsewhere in the file; the specific lines used fell in clean,
legible stretches and were cross-confirmed against independent
citations, but a print spot-check would be worth doing eventually.
- Ajahn Maha Bua's Samaṇa and Arahattamagga – Arahattaphala and Ajahn
Jia Cundo's Gold Wrapped in Rags (all Forest Dhamma) were checked
against FH's EPUB copies. Samaṇa's last chapter reprints Part 1 of
Arahattamagga, so no line is taken from both. Gold Wrapped in Rags
lines are Ajahn Jia's own narration, credited to him even where he
describes Ajahn Mun's teaching.
- Nov 2026 batch from FH's copies: Ajahn Sumedho's The Way It Is, Now
Is the Knowing, Teachings from the Forest, Mindfulness: The Path to
the Deathless and It's Like This; Ajahn Chah's Bodhinyana and
Everything Is Teaching Us; Ajahn Liem's The Ways of the Peaceful and
Knowing the World. Teachings from the Forest reprints three chapters
of Now Is the Knowing, so its lines come from the other chapters.
Knowing the World includes a talk by Ajahn Jundee; only Ajahn Liem's
own words were used.
- Nov 2026 batch from FH's copies of Ajahn Pasanno, Ajahn Amaro,
Ajahn Munindo, Ajahn Jayasaro, Ajahn Viradhammo and Ajahn Sundara
books. The Island is mostly quotation: only the compilers' own
prose was used, credited jointly (preface lines to Ajahn Pasanno).
Lines these books quote from other teachers (Ajahn Chah, forewords)
were left out. Walking the World was checked against page images
because its text layer drops most full stops.
- Nov 2026 batch from FH's copies of Thich Nhat Hanh (The Diamond That
Cuts Through Illusion, The Heart of the Buddha's Teaching, The Heart
of Understanding, True Love), Shunryu Suzuki (Zen Mind, Beginner's
Mind) and Jack Kornfield (After the Ecstasy, the Laundry; The
Eightfold Path for the Householder). Diamond Sutra lines are credited
to the Buddha in Thich Nhat Hanh's translation; FH's copy of that book
lacks the commentary chapters. Lines Kornfield quotes or paraphrases
from other teachers were left out.
- Nov 2026 batch from FH's copies of A Tree in a Forest (Ajahn Chah),
Essential Themes of Buddhist Lectures (Sayadaw U Thittila), Handbook
for Mankind and The Natural Cure for Spiritual Disease (Ajahn
Buddhadasa), Snow in the Summer (Sayadaw U Jotika), The Experience of
Insight (Joseph Goldstein), Facing the Future (Bhikkhu Bodhi) and Real
Love (Sharon Salzberg). A Tree in a Forest was checked against page
images because its text layer drops the letters 'Th'. Lines these
books quote from other writers were left out.

quotes.text: Mind precedes all mental states. Mind is their chief; they are all mind-wrought.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada, v. 1, trans. Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Hatred is never appeased by hatred in this world. By non-hatred alone is hatred appeased. This is a law eternal.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada, v. 5, trans. Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Not to do any evil, to cultivate good, to purify one's mind — this is the teaching of the Buddhas.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada, v. 183, trans. Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: All conditioned things are impermanent — when one sees this with wisdom, one turns away from suffering.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada, v. 277, trans. Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Though one may conquer a thousand times a thousand men in battle, yet he indeed is the noblest victor who conquers himself.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada, v. 103, trans. Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Health is the most precious gain and contentment the greatest wealth. A trustworthy person is the best kinsman, Nibbana the highest bliss.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada, v. 204, trans. Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Just as a solid rock is not shaken by the storm, even so the wise are not affected by praise or blame.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada, v. 81, trans. Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Irrigators regulate the waters, fletchers straighten arrow shafts, carpenters shape wood, and the wise control themselves.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada, v. 80, trans. Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Overcome the angry by non-anger; overcome the wicked by goodness; overcome the miser by generosity; overcome the liar by truth.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada, v. 223, trans. Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Both formerly and now, it is only stress that I describe, and the cessation of stress.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Anuradha Sutta (Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.86), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Just as the great ocean has one taste, the taste of salt, so too this Dhamma and Discipline has one taste: the taste of liberation.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Udāna 5.5, trans. John D. Ireland

quotes.text: Victory begets enmity; the defeated dwell in pain. Happily the peaceful live, discarding both victory and defeat.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada, v. 201, trans. Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: You yourselves must strive; the Buddhas only point the way. Those meditative ones who tread the path are released from the bonds of Mara.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada, v. 276, trans. Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: There is not the slightest difference between cyclic existence and nirvana. There is not the slightest difference between nirvana and cyclic existence.
quotes.author: Nāgārjuna
quotes.source: Mūlamadhyamakakārikā, Ch. 25, v.19, trans. Jay L. Garfield, "The Fundamental Wisdom of the Middle Way" (Oxford University Press, 1995)

quotes.text: All the joy the world contains has come through wishing happiness for others. All the misery the world contains has come through wanting pleasure for oneself.
quotes.author: Śāntideva
quotes.source: The Way of the Bodhisattva, Ch. 8, v.129, trans. Padmakara Translation Group (Shambhala Publications, revised ed. 2006)

quotes.text: All conscious objects are only constructs of consciousness because there are no external objects. They are like a dream.
quotes.author: Asaṅga
quotes.source: The Summary of the Great Vehicle (Mahāyānasaṃgraha), Ch. II.6, trans. John P. Keenan (Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research, rev. 2nd ed. 2003)

quotes.text: He has, in an absolute manner, destroyed all blindness; He has drawn out the world from the mire of transmigration: I render homage to Him, to this teacher of truth, before composing the treatise called the Abhidharmakosa.
quotes.author: Vasubandhu
quotes.source: Abhidharmakośabhāṣyam, Ch. 1, v.1, trans. Louis de La Vallée Poussin / Leo M. Pruden (Asian Humanities Press, 1991)

quotes.text: To find a buddha, you have to see your nature. Whoever sees his or her nature is a buddha.
quotes.author: Bodhidharma
quotes.source: The Zen Teaching of Bodhidharma, "Bloodstream Sermon," trans. Red Pine (North Point Press, 1987)

quotes.text: Bodhi originally has no tree, the mirror also has no stand. Buddha nature is always clean and pure; where is there room for dust?
quotes.author: Huineng
quotes.source: The Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch, trans. Philip B. Yampolsky (Columbia University Press, 1967)

quotes.text: All the Buddhas and all sentient beings are nothing but the One Mind, beside which nothing exists.
quotes.author: Huangbo
quotes.source: The Zen Teaching of Huang Po: On the Transmission of Mind, trans. John Blofeld (Grove Press, 1958)

quotes.text: On your lump of red flesh is a true man without rank who is always going in and out of the face of every one of you. Those who have not yet confirmed this, look, look!
quotes.author: Linji
quotes.source: The Record of Linji, trans. Ruth Fuller Sasaki, ed. Thomas Yūhō Kirchner (University of Hawai'i Press, 2009)

quotes.text: If you let go a little, you will have a little peace. If you let go a lot, you will have a lot of peace. And if you let go completely, you will have complete peace.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: No Ajahn Chah: Reflections

quotes.text: Peace is within oneself to be found in the same place as agitation and suffering. It is not found in a forest or on a hilltop, nor is it given by a teacher. Where you experience suffering, you can also find freedom from suffering.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: No Ajahn Chah: Reflections

quotes.text: If your mind is peaceful, you are peaceful, and then wherever you go, you will not have any problems.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Still Forest Pool

quotes.text: Do not try to become anything. Do not make yourself into anything. Do not be a meditator. Do not become enlightened.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Still Forest Pool

quotes.text: Your practice now is patience.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Recorded talk, quoted in the Ajahn Pasanno Archive, Abhayagiri Monastery

quotes.text: It's the suffering that awakens you.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Recorded talk, quoted in the Ajahn Pasanno Archive, Abhayagiri Monastery

quotes.text: Enlightenment is not something you can find by searching. It's a matter of stopping.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Still Forest Pool

quotes.text: The heart of the path is so simple. No need for long explanations. Give up clinging to love and hate, just rest with things as they are.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Still Forest Pool, "The Simple Path"

quotes.text: There are two kinds of suffering: the suffering that leads to more suffering and the suffering that leads to the end of suffering.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Still Forest Pool, "Happiness and Suffering"

quotes.text: To want something that's not present, something you don't have, is suffering.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Remembering Ajahn Chah Weekend talk (2001), Ajahn Pasanno Archive, Abhayagiri Monastery

quotes.text: When I saw Luang Por Chah when he had his stroke, I felt an almost unbearable sense of grief and loss. Then I remembered, 'This is the way it is.'
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Remembering Ajahn Chah Weekend talk (2001), Ajahn Pasanno Archive, Abhayagiri Monastery

quotes.text: The mind is like space, there's room in it for everything or nothing.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Now Is the Knowing, "Happiness, Unhappiness and Nibbana" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: So recognize that it's the attachment that causes the suffering, attaching to conditions and expecting them to be more than what they are.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Now Is the Knowing, "Happiness, Unhappiness and Nibbana" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: Careful patience is the fastest way!
quotes.author: Ajahn Brahm
quotes.source: Mindfulness, Bliss, and Beyond: A Meditator's Handbook

quotes.text: Silence is so much more productive of wisdom and clarity than thinking.
quotes.author: Ajahn Brahm
quotes.source: Mindfulness, Bliss, and Beyond: A Meditator's Handbook, "Silence Is Delightful"

quotes.text: It is the high value that one gives to one's own thoughts that is the main obstacle to silent awareness.
quotes.author: Ajahn Brahm
quotes.source: Mindfulness, Bliss, and Beyond: A Meditator's Handbook

quotes.text: Virtue — normalcy — is like rock, which is solid and forms the basis of the ground. No matter how much the wind may buffet and blow, rock doesn't waver or flinch.
quotes.author: Ajahn Mun Bhuridatta
quotes.source: A Heart Released, § 2, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: An unconfused person doesn't have to look for anything. Only a confused person has to go looking. The more he goes looking, the further he gets lost.
quotes.author: Ajahn Mun Bhuridatta
quotes.source: A Heart Released, § 1, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: When a leaf grows yellow and falls from the tree, for instance, it's showing you the truth of inconstancy.
quotes.author: Ajahn Mun Bhuridatta
quotes.source: A Heart Released, § 8, "The Ever-present Truth," trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: You have to make the Dhamma your life, and your life into Dhamma if you want to succeed.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Food for Thought: Eighteen Talks on the Training of the Heart, "First Things First," trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Stick to your duties as you always have. Don't let your goodness suffer because of these eight ways of the world.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Food for Thought: Eighteen Talks on the Training of the Heart, "First Things First," trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: So no matter how good or bad other people may be, we don't store it up in our mind to give rise to feelings of like or dislike. Dismiss it completely as being their business and none of ours.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Inner Strength & Parting Gifts: Talks by Ajaan Lee Dhammadharo, "The Last Sermon," trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: We should see and understand that nothing is ours. Nothing belongs to us.
quotes.author: Ajahn Liem Thitadhammo
quotes.source: "The Lightness of Letting Go," Dhamma talk at Dhammagiri Forest Hermitage, trans. Alex Oliver (15 March 2023)

quotes.text: The suffering of the mind is really like a disease. Desire, never being satisfied, never knowing enough, is the virus which causes it. And peace and seclusion is the medicine which cures the illness.
quotes.author: Ajahn Liem Thitadhammo
quotes.source: The Ways of the Peaceful, p. 9; trans. Wat Nong Pah Pong (2007)

quotes.text: Feelings are just feelings, happiness is just happiness, suffering is just suffering. Only that. Having arisen, it all ceases.
quotes.author: Ajahn Liem Thitadhammo
quotes.source: The Ways of the Peaceful, p. 123; trans. Wat Nong Pah Pong (2007)

quotes.text: Our mind is like a flame when the wind is stilled. The flame is unmoved and upright in itself and blazes light into all directions, when we are fully present.
quotes.author: Ajahn Liem Thitadhammo
quotes.source: The Ways of the Peaceful, p. 116; trans. Wat Nong Pah Pong (2007)

quotes.text: You need to keep in mind that the source of peace and the attainment to perfection is to be found exactly where dukkha is.
quotes.author: Ajahn Liem Thitadhammo
quotes.source: The Ways of the Peaceful, p. 44; trans. Wat Nong Pah Pong (2007)

quotes.text: Whenever you don’t get what you like, take it as a training in the Dhamma. At least you get some experience and training with the Dhamma of patient endurance.
quotes.author: Ajahn Liem Thitadhammo
quotes.source: The Ways of the Peaceful, p. 59; trans. Wat Nong Pah Pong (2007)

quotes.text: If we get little, that’s enough. If we get much, that’s enough. Even if we don’t get anything at all – that’s enough.
quotes.author: Ajahn Liem Thitadhammo
quotes.source: The Ways of the Peaceful, p. 30; trans. Wat Nong Pah Pong (2007)

quotes.text: The guests that come to our monastery are agantukas — only visitors, just like these visiting mental states that arise in our minds. Some make us laugh, some we delight in, while others bring up aversion and disappointment.
quotes.author: Ajahn Liem Thitadhammo
quotes.source: Knowing the World, p. 9; Dhamma talk at Na Uyana Forest Monastery, Sri Lanka, March 2013; trans. Wat Pah Nanachat

quotes.text: Neither good nor bad. Neither heavy nor light. Neither black nor white. Neither happy nor sad. Just nature pure and simple. This is the normal state of the mind which gives rise to peace.
quotes.author: Ajahn Liem Thitadhammo
quotes.source: Knowing the World, p. 12; Dhamma talk at Na Uyana Forest Monastery, Sri Lanka, March 2013; trans. Wat Pah Nanachat

quotes.text: The changes in our lives are just natural because nature changes.
quotes.author: Ajahn Liem Thitadhammo
quotes.source: Knowing the World, p. 17; Dhamma talk at Na Uyana Forest Monastery, Sri Lanka, March 2013; trans. Wat Pah Nanachat

quotes.text: Delight comes from desire. Satisfaction comes from desire. Aversion and dissatisfaction come from desire.
quotes.author: Ajahn Liem Thitadhammo
quotes.source: Knowing the World, p. 7; Dhamma talk at Na Uyana Forest Monastery, Sri Lanka, March 2013; trans. Wat Pah Nanachat

quotes.text: If I hadn’t seen the impurities still in the mind, then I wouldn’t have known how it needed further purifying.
quotes.author: Ajahn Liem Thitadhammo
quotes.source: Knowing the World, p. 20; Dhamma talk at Na Uyana Forest Monastery, Sri Lanka, March 2013; trans. Wat Pah Nanachat

quotes.text: Keep abandoning delight and aversion from your mind. See everything as not your self or belonging to you. We have no real power or control over our life or the world.
quotes.author: Ajahn Liem Thitadhammo
quotes.source: Knowing the World, p. 21; Dhamma talk at Na Uyana Forest Monastery, Sri Lanka, March 2013; trans. Wat Pah Nanachat

quotes.text: There's no way that you can have anger and resentment and feel peaceful and happy.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: Thanksgiving Retreat 2010, Session 1 (Nov. 20, 2010), The Ajahn Pasanno Question and Story Archive, Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery

quotes.text: This condition, this experience, this happiness or suffering is impermanent; this, too, will change.
quotes.author: Ajahn Ñāṇadhammo
quotes.source: "The Power of Faith," Dhamma talk at Wat Pah Nanachat, 27 September 2002 (Wat Pah Nanachat, 2003)

quotes.text: Don't simply sit and keep on sitting, or walk and keep on walking. You have to remember to notice what results and benefits you get from your efforts as well.
quotes.author: Ajahn Maha Bua
quotes.source: Things As They Are: A Collection of Talks on the Training of the Mind, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu (Forest Dhamma Books)

quotes.text: All dhammas exist here, within each of us and the one that knows Dhamma is the heart or mind.
quotes.author: Ajahn Tate
quotes.source: The Autobiography of a Forest Monk, "Parents' Life Story," trans. Bhikkhu Ariyesako (1996)

quotes.text: As ultimate reality emerges, concepts submerge. As concepts emerge, ultimate reality submerges.
quotes.author: Mahasi Sayadaw
quotes.source: Manual of Insight

quotes.text: The practice of Vipassana, or insight meditation, was described by the Buddha as the direct way for the overcoming of sorrow and grief and for realizing Nibbana, the state of perfect liberation from suffering.
quotes.author: Mahasi Sayadaw
quotes.source: Practical Insight Meditation: Basic and Progressive Stages

quotes.text: Sufferings of this nature are not overcome by material means; they can be overcome only mind training and mental development.
quotes.author: Mahasi Sayadaw
quotes.source: Practical Insight Meditation: Basic and Progressive Stages, Preface

quotes.text: We do not practice meditation to gain admiration from anyone. Rather, we practice to contribute to peace in the world.
quotes.author: Sayadaw U Pandita
quotes.source: In This Very Life: Liberation Teachings of the Buddha, "Basic Morality & Meditation Instructions" (Wisdom Publications, 1992)

quotes.text: Mindfulness is something like a stone hitting a wall.
quotes.author: Sayadaw U Silananda
quotes.source: The Four Foundations of Mindfulness, Introduction (Wisdom Publications, 2002)

quotes.text: Wanting to understand is wisdom, wanting a result is greed.
quotes.author: Sayadaw U Tejaniya
quotes.source: "The Wise Investigator," interview in Tricycle magazine, Winter 2007

quotes.text: It's not the posture that's meditating; it's the mind.
quotes.author: Sayadaw U Tejaniya
quotes.source: "The Wise Investigator," interview in Tricycle magazine, Winter 2007

quotes.text: Awareness alone is not enough! Having a desire to really understand what is going on is much more important than just trying to be aware.
quotes.author: Sayadaw U Tejaniya
quotes.source: Awareness Alone Is Not Enough

quotes.text: Patience brings forth peace, success, happiness and security.
quotes.author: Sayadaw U Thittila
quotes.source: Essential Themes of Buddhist Lectures, "Patience", p. 338

quotes.text: We may live in this world quite happily if we are not attached to it by foolish desire.
quotes.author: Sayadaw U Thittila
quotes.source: Essential Themes of Buddhist Lectures, p. 133

quotes.text: Meditation is mental training, and from a trained mind spring right thoughts, words and deeds.
quotes.author: Sayadaw U Thittila
quotes.source: Essential Themes of Buddhist Lectures, p. 163

quotes.text: What we call happiness or pleasure in the world, is merely gratification of some desire, but no sooner is the desired thing gained than it begins to be scorned.
quotes.author: Sayadaw U Thittila
quotes.source: Essential Themes of Buddhist Lectures, p. 201

quotes.text: Impermanence is a suitable subject for everyone. Suffering is too depressing for certain natures to meditate on.
quotes.author: Sayadaw U Thittila
quotes.source: Essential Themes of Buddhist Lectures, "Meditation", p. 234

quotes.text: Don’t use force. Keep your mind soft. Happiness is having a quiet mind, and being completely mindful, so mindful that there is no thought, no sense of I.
quotes.author: Sayadaw U Jotika
quotes.source: Snow in the Summer

quotes.text: Only deep understanding of attachment can free the mind of it. If you force your mind to let go of attachment without really seeing the nature of it, it will come back very soon.
quotes.author: Sayadaw U Jotika
quotes.source: Snow in the Summer

quotes.text: Defilements make life complicated. Without greed, desire, and attachment you can live a simple life like Ryokan.
quotes.author: Sayadaw U Jotika
quotes.source: Snow in the Summer, "Life, Living and Death"

quotes.text: I am not trying to be somebody. I just try my best to understand whatever is happening in my life, in my mind, in my heart. No name and no fame; when I die nothing will remain.
quotes.author: Sayadaw U Jotika
quotes.source: Snow in the Summer

quotes.text: We use mindfulness as a painkiller. Only when life becomes too painful do we want to go to a quiet place and meditate. Otherwise we are quite content with distractions.
quotes.author: Sayadaw U Jotika
quotes.source: Snow in the Summer, "Mind, Mindfulness and Meditation"

quotes.text: So the Buddhist attitude toward life cultivates samvega — a clear acceptance of the meaninglessness of the cycle of birth, aging, and death — and develops it into pasada: a confident path to the Deathless.
quotes.author: Thanissaro Bhikkhu
quotes.source: "Affirming the Truths of the Heart: The Buddhist Teachings on Samvega & Pasada," in Noble Strategy: Essays on the Buddhist Path (1997)

quotes.text: For real security always lies on the side of truth, not on the side of comfort.
quotes.author: Bhikkhu Bodhi
quotes.source: The Noble Eightfold Path: The Way to the End of Suffering, Ch. III, "Right Intention"

quotes.text: The present moment is the only moment available to us, and it is the door to all moments.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: Peace Is Every Step

quotes.text: Walk as if you are kissing the Earth with your feet.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: Peace Is Every Step

quotes.text: Because you are alive, everything is possible.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: Being Peace

quotes.text: The most precious gift we can offer others is our presence.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: Peace Is Every Step

quotes.text: People have a hard time letting go of their suffering. Out of a fear of the unknown, they prefer suffering that is familiar.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: Peace Is Every Step

quotes.text: Feelings come and go like clouds in a windy sky. Conscious breathing is my anchor.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: Being Peace

quotes.text: Every breath we take, every step we make, can be filled with peace, joy, and serenity.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: Peace Is Every Step

quotes.text: Breathing in, I calm body and mind. Breathing out, I smile.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: Present Moment Wonderful Moment

quotes.text: There are two ways to wash the dishes. The first is to wash the dishes in order to have clean dishes and the second is to wash the dishes in order to wash the dishes.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: The Miracle of Mindfulness: An Introduction to the Practice of Meditation

quotes.text: The only thing worthy of you is compassion—invincible, limitless, unconditional.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: The Diamond That Cuts Through Illusion, from the poem "Recommendation"

quotes.text: Even if the world is shattered, your smile will never vanish.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: The Diamond That Cuts Through Illusion, poem

quotes.text: Letting go gives us freedom, and freedom is the only condition for happiness. If, in our heart, we still cling to anything — anger, anxiety, or possessions — we cannot be free.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: The Heart of the Buddha's Teaching, "Right Mindfulness"

quotes.text: Impermanence is what makes transformation possible. We should learn to say, "Long live impermanence." Thanks to impermanence, we can change suffering into joy.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: The Heart of the Buddha's Teaching, "The Three Dharma Seals"

quotes.text: The practice of mindful living should be joyful and pleasant. If you breathe in and out and feel joy and peace, that is Right Diligence.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: The Heart of the Buddha's Teaching, "Right Diligence"

quotes.text: Our suffering is us, and we need to treat it with kindness and nonviolence.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: The Heart of the Buddha's Teaching, "Touching Our Suffering"

quotes.text: With compassion in our heart, every thought, word, and deed can bring about a miracle.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: The Heart of the Buddha's Teaching, "The Four Immeasurable Minds"

quotes.text: Some kinds of happiness actually destroy our body, our mind, and our relationships. Freedom from craving is an important practice.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: The Heart of the Buddha's Teaching, "The Six Paramitas"

quotes.text: Emptiness is impermanence, it is change. We should not complain about impermanence, because without impermanence nothing is possible.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: The Heart of Understanding: Commentaries on the Prajñaparamita Heart Sutra

quotes.text: The word emptiness should not scare us. It is a wonderful word. To be empty does not mean non-existent.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: The Heart of Understanding: Commentaries on the Prajñaparamita Heart Sutra

quotes.text: The wave is full of water, but it is empty of a separate self.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: The Heart of Understanding: Commentaries on the Prajñaparamita Heart Sutra

quotes.text: If we practice walking meditation, we walk just for walking, not to arrive.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: The Heart of Understanding: Commentaries on the Prajñaparamita Heart Sutra

quotes.text: To smile is not to smile only for yourself; the world will change because of your smile.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: The Heart of Understanding: Commentaries on the Prajñaparamita Heart Sutra

quotes.text: Form is empty of a separate self, but it is full of everything in the cosmos.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: The Heart of Understanding: Commentaries on the Prajñaparamita Heart Sutra

quotes.text: To meditate is to bring body and mind back to the present moment so that you do not miss your appointment with life.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: True Love: A Practice for Awakening the Heart, "Recognizing the Presence of the Other"

quotes.text: Those who have practiced Buddhist meditation know that meditating is above all being present: to yourself, to those you love, to life.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: True Love: A Practice for Awakening the Heart, "Love Is Being There"

quotes.text: Training is needed in order to love properly; and to be able to give happiness and joy, you must practice deep looking directed toward the person you love.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: True Love: A Practice for Awakening the Heart, "The Four Aspects of Love"

quotes.text: To be able to provide help, we have to have a little calm, a little joy, a little compassion in ourselves.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: True Love: A Practice for Awakening the Heart, "Restoring Peace within Yourself"

quotes.text: Whatever you do mindfully is meditation.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: True Love: A Practice for Awakening the Heart, "Recognizing the Presence of the Other"

quotes.text: Meditation is the practice of looking deeply into the nature of your suffering and your joy.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: True Love: A Practice for Awakening the Heart, "Learning to Speak with Love Again"

quotes.text: Things are more dangerous than fire because we can at least see a fire blazing away and so don't go too close to it, whereas all things are a fire we can't see.
quotes.author: Ajahn Buddhadasa
quotes.source: Handbook for Mankind, Ch. 2, "The True Nature of Things," trans. Ariyananda Bhikkhu (Roderick S. Bucknell)

quotes.text: When the mind is free from attachment, there is nothing to bind it and make it a slave of the world.
quotes.author: Ajahn Buddhadasa
quotes.source: Handbook for Mankind, trans. Roderick Bucknell, p. 56

quotes.text: With the insight that nothing is worth getting or being constantly present, the mind loses all desire for the things it once used to grasp at and cling to.
quotes.author: Ajahn Buddhadasa
quotes.source: Handbook for Mankind, trans. Roderick Bucknell, p. 95

quotes.text: The single phrase “empty of self” sums up the words “impermanent (aniccā), unsatisfactory (dukkha) and not self (anattā)”.
quotes.author: Ajahn Buddhadasa
quotes.source: Handbook for Mankind, trans. Roderick Bucknell, p. 35

quotes.text: In saying that all things are impermanent we mean that things change perpetually, there being no entity or self that remains unchanged for even an instant.
quotes.author: Ajahn Buddhadasa
quotes.source: Handbook for Mankind, trans. Roderick Bucknell, p. 25

quotes.text: Gain and loss, happiness and sorrow, amount in effect to mental restlessness or instability; they set the mind spinning.
quotes.author: Ajahn Buddhadasa
quotes.source: Handbook for Mankind, trans. Roderick Bucknell, p. 70

quotes.text: To be truly human is to be above all problems. Study and learn in order to be completely human.
quotes.author: Ajahn Buddhadasa
quotes.source: The Natural Cure for Spiritual Disease, talk I, p. 18

quotes.text: Make the mind empty, free, and spotless, so that you can hear something new.
quotes.author: Ajahn Buddhadasa
quotes.source: The Natural Cure for Spiritual Disease, talk I, p. 11

quotes.text: When we’re afraid we become helpless. When there is fear, we lose our mindfulness and wisdom (sati-panna), and our ability to struggle with problems and protect ourselves.
quotes.author: Ajahn Buddhadasa
quotes.source: The Natural Cure for Spiritual Disease, talk III, p. 48

quotes.text: Physical disease pierces the body; spiritual disease stabs the mind or spirit. Dhamma is the latter’s remedy.
quotes.author: Ajahn Buddhadasa
quotes.source: The Natural Cure for Spiritual Disease, talk I, p. 12

quotes.text: When the mind keeps running all over the world, keeps getting involved in everything, it is impossible to perform even a simple task like writing a letter.
quotes.author: Ajahn Buddhadasa
quotes.source: The Natural Cure for Spiritual Disease, talk III, p. 43

quotes.text: It is not like we need to become free. It is a matter of discovering that quality of being that is inherently unhindered and unbounded.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Small Boat, Great Mountain: Theravadan Reflections on the Natural Great Perfection, Ch. 1, "The Search for Freedom"

quotes.text: It would be a sad thing to put all our hopes for happiness into a future that never arrives.
quotes.author: Ajahn Jayasaro
quotes.source: Without and Within: Questions and Answers on the Teachings of Theravāda Buddhism

quotes.text: Letting go is about gaining ease and clarity – and because of these one consequently doesn't need a whole lot of stuff to lift the heart.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sucitto
quotes.source: Meditation: A Way of Awakening, "Preliminaries — Three Basic Attitudes for Meditation," Cittaviveka

quotes.text: What we face every day is unpredictable. Things happen due to multiple causes and conditions, since we live in a conditional and impermanent world. Mindfulness is our emergency kit, readily available at any time.
quotes.author: Bhante Henepola Gunaratana
quotes.source: Mindfulness in Plain English, Ch. 5, "The Practice"

quotes.text: Mind is the very element in and through which we live, yet it is what is most elusive and mysterious. Bare Attention, however, by first attending patiently to the basic facts of the mental processes, is capable of shedding light on mind's mysterious darkness, and of obtaining a firm hold on its elusive flow.
quotes.author: Nyanaponika Thera
quotes.source: The Heart of Buddhist Meditation, Ch. 2, "Mindfulness and Clear Comprehension" (Buddhist Publication Society)

quotes.text: A guiding principle—the foremost, in fact—has throughout been avoidance of misrepresentation or distortion; for the ideal translation (which has yet to be made) should, like a looking glass, not discolour or blur or warp the original which it reflects.
quotes.author: Bhikkhu Ñāṇamoli
quotes.source: The Path of Purification (Visuddhimagga), Translator's Preface, trans. Bhikkhu Ñāṇamoli (Buddhist Publication Society, 1956)

quotes.text: In the end, however, all four satipaṭṭhānas partake of the same essence. Each of them leads to realisation, like different gateways leading to the same city.
quotes.author: Bhikkhu Analayo
quotes.source: Satipaṭṭhāna: The Direct Path to Realization

quotes.text: Do you see? It's not what you own that is the problem. The problem is how much you are attached to it. The problem is not so much desire, but clinging. If you want to hold water, you have to hold it with cupped hands. If you make a tight fist, it runs away. Clinging and attachment bring us great suffering. We think attachment is love, but it is not.
quotes.author: Jetsunma Tenzin Palmo
quotes.source: Reflections on a Mountain Lake

quotes.text: Nothing in the whole universe is comparable to the mind or can take its place. Everything is mind-made.
quotes.author: Ayya Khema
quotes.source: Being Nobody, Going Nowhere: Meditations on the Buddhist Path, Ch. 1, "Meditation—Why and How" (Wisdom Publications, 1987)

quotes.text: To stay with that shakiness—to stay with a broken heart, with a rumbling stomach, with the feeling of hopelessness and wanting to get revenge—that is the path of true awakening. Sticking with that uncertainty, getting the knack of relaxing in the midst of chaos, learning not to panic—this is the spiritual path.
quotes.author: Pema Chödrön
quotes.source: When Things Fall Apart: Heart Advice for Difficult Times

quotes.text: Underneath our ordinary lives, underneath all the talking we do, all the moving we do, all the thoughts in our minds, there's a fundamental groundlessness.
quotes.author: Pema Chödrön
quotes.source: When Things Fall Apart: Heart Advice for Difficult Times

quotes.text: Confusion, I was taught, is the beginning of understanding, the first stage of letting go of the neuronal gossip that used to keep you chained to very specific ideas about who you are and what you're capable of.
quotes.author: Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche
quotes.source: The Joy of Living: Unlocking the Secret and Science of Happiness

quotes.text: There is not a single being in samsara, this immense ocean of suffering, who in the course of time without beginning has never been our father or mother.
quotes.author: Patrul Rinpoche
quotes.source: The Words of My Perfect Teacher, trans. Padmakara Translation Group

quotes.text: To amass a multitude of profound texts, such as scriptures, commentaries and oral instructions, without practicing them, will be of no benefit at the time of death. 'To watch your mind' is my heart advice.
quotes.author: Longchenpa
quotes.source: Thirty Pieces of Heart Advice, trans. Daniela Hartmann (Lotsawa House, 2014)

quotes.text: Realization of the pure awareness that transcends the mind is the specialty of the Great Perfection.
quotes.author: Jigme Lingpa
quotes.source: Yeshe Lama, trans. Lama Chonam & Sangye Khandro (Snow Lion Publications, 2013)

quotes.text: Do not blame your past karma; instead, be someone who purely and flawlessly practices the Dharma. Do not blame temporary negative circumstances; instead, be someone who remains steadfast in the face of whatever circumstances may arise.
quotes.author: Dudjom Rinpoche
quotes.source: Wisdom Nectar: Dudjom Rinpoche's Heart Advice, p. 58, trans. Ron Garry (Snow Lion Publications / Tsadra Foundation, 2011)

quotes.text: Even if a person is a lowly beggar, if they are in harmony with the Dharma they can be called a great person who is a holder of the teachings.
quotes.author: Chatral Rinpoche
quotes.source: Compassionate Action: The Teachings of Chatral Rinpoche, trans. Zach Larson (Snow Lion Publications, 2005)

quotes.text: We'll discover a sense of confidence that isn't rooted in arrogance or pride. We'll realize that we're always sheltered, always safe, and always home.
quotes.author: Tsoknyi Rinpoche
quotes.source: Open Heart, Open Mind: A Guide to Inner Transformation, with Eric Swanson (Harmony/Random House, 2012)

quotes.text: True virtue, real goodness, is created through recognizing our buddha nature, our natural state. Recognize your mind, and in the absence of any concrete thing, rest loosely.
quotes.author: Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche
quotes.source: As It Is, Volume II, trans. Erik Pema Kunsang, ed. Marcia Schmidt & Kerry Moran (Rangjung Yeshe Publications, 2000)

quotes.text: It is important to see that the main point of any spiritual practice is to step out of the bureaucracy of ego.
quotes.author: Chögyam Trungpa
quotes.source: Cutting Through Spiritual Materialism, "Spiritual Materialism" (Shambhala Publications, 1973)

quotes.text: Compassion releases others from your struggle to make them conform to your wishes. There is a great deal of kindness in giving others the freedom to evolve naturally as they are.
quotes.author: Jetsun Khandro Rinpoche
quotes.source: How Not to Miss the Point: The Buddha's Wisdom for a Life Well Lived (Shambhala Publications, 2025)

quotes.text: True ethics is not just about following some old scriptures nor about adhering to a behavior code dictated by any given society. Its roots lie in each of us—empathy and compassion.
quotes.author: Anam Thubten
quotes.source: "Ethics Are the Heart of Spiritual Practice," Lion's Roar (2026)

quotes.text: There is no danger of disrupting something important when we change our dreams. All we disrupt is our ignorance.
quotes.author: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
quotes.source: The Tibetan Yogas of Dream and Sleep: Practices for Awakening, 2nd ed. (Shambhala Publications, 1998/2022)

quotes.text: Buddhists venerate wisdom above all else. Wisdom surpasses morality, love, common sense, tolerance, and vegetarianism.
quotes.author: Dzongsar Khyentse Rinpoche
quotes.source: What Makes You Not a Buddhist (Shambhala Publications, 2007)

quotes.text: In the beginner's mind there are many possibilities, but in the expert's there are few.
quotes.author: Shunryu Suzuki
quotes.source: Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind (1970)

quotes.text: Doing something is expressing our own nature. We do not exist for the sake of something else. We exist for the sake of ourselves.
quotes.author: Shunryu Suzuki
quotes.source: Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind (1970), "Posture"

quotes.text: Shikantaza, our zazen, is just to be ourselves. When we do not expect anything we can be ourselves.
quotes.author: Shunryu Suzuki
quotes.source: Not Always So: Practicing the True Spirit of Zen, "Shikantaza: Living Fully in Each Moment"

quotes.text: When we have no thought of achievement, no thought of self, we are true beginners. Then we can really learn something. The beginner’s mind is the mind of compassion.
quotes.author: Shunryu Suzuki
quotes.source: Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind (1970), "Prologue: Beginner's Mind"

quotes.text: Mindfulness is, at the same time, wisdom. By wisdom we do not mean some particular faculty or philosophy. It is the readiness of the mind that is wisdom.
quotes.author: Shunryu Suzuki
quotes.source: Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind (1970), "Readiness, Mindfulness"

quotes.text: Do not try to stop your mind, but leave everything as it is.
quotes.author: Shunryu Suzuki
quotes.source: Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind (1970), "Beyond Consciousness"

quotes.text: Just continue in your calm, ordinary practice and your character will be built up.
quotes.author: Shunryu Suzuki
quotes.source: Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind (1970), "Zen and Excitement"

quotes.text: We do not seek for something besides ourselves. We should find the truth in this world, through our difficulties, through our suffering.
quotes.author: Shunryu Suzuki
quotes.source: Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind (1970), "Transiency"

quotes.text: We must have beginner’s mind, free from possessing anything, a mind that knows everything is in flowing change. Nothing exists but momentarily in its present form and color.
quotes.author: Shunryu Suzuki
quotes.source: Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind (1970), "Epilogue: Zen Mind"

quotes.text: To study the buddha way is to study the self. To study the self is to forget the self. To forget the self is to be actualized by myriad things.
quotes.author: Dogen
quotes.source: Shobogenzo, "Genjokoan," in Moon in a Dewdrop, trans. Robert Aitken and Kazuaki Tanahashi

quotes.text: You should therefore cease from practice based on intellectual understanding, pursuing words and following after speech, and learn the backward step that turns your light inward to illuminate your self. Body and mind will drop away of themselves, and your original face will manifest itself.
quotes.author: Dogen
quotes.source: Fukanzazengi ("Universal Recommendation for Zazen"), trans. Norman Waddell and Abe Masao, The Eastern Buddhist, New Series 6, no. 2 (1973)

quotes.text: So-called great mind is, in its spirit, like a great mountain or a great sea: it has no partiality and no factionalism.
quotes.author: Dogen
quotes.source: Tenzo Kyokun ("Instructions for the Cook"), trans. Griffith Foulk, in Nothing Is Hidden: Essays on Zen Master Dogen's Instructions for the Cook (Weatherhill, 2001)

quotes.text: All beings by nature are Buddha, as ice by nature is water. Apart from water there is no ice; apart from beings, no Buddha.
quotes.author: Hakuin Ekaku
quotes.source: Song of Zazen (Zazen Wasan), trans. D.T. Suzuki, Manual of Zen Buddhism

quotes.text: Not a single one of you people at this meeting is unenlightened. Right now, you're all sitting before me as Buddhas. Each of you received the Buddha-mind from your mothers when you were born, and nothing else.
quotes.author: Bankei Yōtaku
quotes.source: The Unborn: The Life and Teachings of Zen Master Bankei, 1622–1693, trans. Norman Waddell, "The Ryumon-ji Sermons"

quotes.text: In the world, it's always about winning or losing, plus or minus. Yet in Zazen, it's about nothing. It's good for nothing. That's why it is the greatest and most all-inclusive thing there is.
quotes.author: Kōdō Sawaki
quotes.source: To You: Zen Sayings of Kodo Sawaki, trans. Jesse Haasch and Muhō Nölke

quotes.text: Left behind by the thief— / The moon / In the window.
quotes.author: Ryōkan
quotes.source: Dewdrops on a Lotus Leaf: Zen Poems of Ryokan, trans. John Stevens

quotes.text: Even if you sit until your seat breaks through, even if you persevere mindless of fatigue, even if you are a person of lofty deeds and pure behavior, if you haven't reached this realm of satori, you still can't get out of the prison of the world.
quotes.author: Keizan Jōkin
quotes.source: Transmission of Light (Denkoroku), trans. Thomas Cleary (North Point Press, 1990)

quotes.text: The entrance into Zen is the grasping of one's essential nature. It is absolutely impossible, however, to come to a clear understanding of our essential nature by any intellectual or philosophical method. It is accomplished only by the experience of self-realization through zazen.
quotes.author: Kōun Yamada
quotes.source: The Gateless Gate, Case 1 commentary (Wisdom Publications, 2004 ed.)

quotes.text: We must save the world, but we can only save it by saving little pieces of it, each of us using his or her own small, partial ability.
quotes.author: Robert Aitken
quotes.source: The Mind of Clover: Essays in Zen Buddhist Ethics (North Point Press, 1984)

quotes.text: The pitfall is always within yourself. This very body and mind is the Way. You are complete to begin with. There is no gap, but you think there is.
quotes.author: Taizan Maezumi
quotes.source: Appreciate Your Life: The Essence of Zen Practice, ed. Wendy Egyoku Nakao & Eve Myonen Marko (Shambhala Publications, 2001)

quotes.text: In my view, we can't heal ourselves or other people unless we bear witness. In the Zen Peacemaker Order we stress bearing witness to the wholeness of life, to every aspect of the situation that arises.
quotes.author: Bernie Glassman
quotes.source: Bearing Witness: A Zen Master's Lessons in Making Peace (Bell Tower, 1998)

quotes.text: The life of the Buddha is the manifestation of compassion, but if you do not engage it, it does nothing. It all depends on you.
quotes.author: John Daido Loori
quotes.source: The Eight Gates of Zen: A Program of Zen Training (Dharma Communications/Shambhala, 2002)

quotes.text: All of us, regardless of whether we realize it or not, are living out the self as the whole universe.
quotes.author: Kosho Uchiyama
quotes.source: Opening the Hand of Thought: Foundations of Zen Buddhist Practice (Wisdom Publications, 2004)

quotes.text: This morning as I wake, I vow with all beings to see each thing as it is and not to forsake the world.
quotes.author: Zenkei Blanche Hartman
quotes.source: Seeds for a Boundless Life: Zen Teachings from the Heart (Shambhala Publications, 2015)

quotes.text: The practice has become that simple: not-clinging, and then moments of recognizing clinging, and then not-clinging, and so on.
quotes.author: Joseph Goldstein
quotes.source: "One Dharma, The Emerging Western Buddhism," interview in Inquiring Mind, Vol. 18 No. 2, Spring 2002

quotes.text: Right thought means becoming aware of sense desires and letting them go. The more we let go, the lighter the mind becomes.
quotes.author: Joseph Goldstein
quotes.source: The Experience of Insight, "Second Evening", p. 9

quotes.text: We don’t have to figure out the causes of our problems, we have to let go of them.
quotes.author: Joseph Goldstein
quotes.source: The Experience of Insight, "Ninth Evening", p. 51

quotes.text: Insight comes from mindfulness, and either we’re aware of what’s happening or not. There’s no way of being mindfully wrong.
quotes.author: Joseph Goldstein
quotes.source: The Experience of Insight, p. 59

quotes.text: Thoughts should not be treated as obstacles or hindrances. They are just another object of mindfulness, another object of meditation.
quotes.author: Joseph Goldstein
quotes.source: The Experience of Insight, p. 25

quotes.text: In letting go of attachment to our own preconceptions, in that silence of mind, the whole Dharma is revealed.
quotes.author: Joseph Goldstein
quotes.source: The Experience of Insight, "Twenty-Ninth Evening", p. 132

quotes.text: Nirvana appears when we let go, when we live in the reality of the present. Sorrow arises when the mind and heart are caught in greed, hatred, and delusion. Nirvana appears in their absence.
quotes.author: Jack Kornfield
quotes.source: "The Wise Heart," interview in Tricycle magazine, Summer 2008

quotes.text: At the root of suffering is a small heart, frightened to be here, afraid to trust the river of change, to let go in this changing world.
quotes.author: Jack Kornfield
quotes.source: After the Ecstasy, the Laundry, "The Wisdom of Not Knowing"

quotes.text: The truth is that in spiritual life, our awareness of suffering actually increases over the years. We see and know more clearly the sorrows of the world.
quotes.author: Jack Kornfield
quotes.source: After the Ecstasy, the Laundry, "Stretching the Heart’s Mercy"

quotes.text: The point of spiritual practice is not to wait for illness or death to awaken us, but to draw on the life and health we have now to bring peace to our body, heart, and mind.
quotes.author: Jack Kornfield
quotes.source: After the Ecstasy, the Laundry, "Embodied Courage"

quotes.text: Though it sounds simple, letting go is also an advanced practice. It is demanded in the greatest trials of our lives and in our final moments.
quotes.author: Jack Kornfield
quotes.source: After the Ecstasy, the Laundry, "The Secret Embrace"

quotes.text: We armor and defend the heart not only against the world, but against ourselves. Some of us fear sadness, others fear joy; some fear weakness, others fear strength.
quotes.author: Jack Kornfield
quotes.source: After the Ecstasy, the Laundry, "Weeping Buddha, Wrathful Buddha"

quotes.text: We can bow to both beauty and suffering, to our entanglements and confusion, to our fears and to the injustices of the world. Honoring the truth in this way is the path to freedom.
quotes.author: Jack Kornfield
quotes.source: After the Ecstasy, the Laundry, "An Opening Bow"

quotes.text: The opposite of greed is generosity; the opposite of hatred is love; the opposite of delusion is awareness.
quotes.author: Jack Kornfield
quotes.source: The Eightfold Path for the Householder (talks, 1995), "Right Action", p. 47

quotes.text: Fear is always about something that hasn’t come, so is worry, so is desire.
quotes.author: Jack Kornfield
quotes.source: The Eightfold Path for the Householder (talks, 1995), "Right Concentration", p. 89

quotes.text: In the end what one discovers is that mindfulness and love are the same thing.
quotes.author: Jack Kornfield
quotes.source: The Eightfold Path for the Householder (talks, 1995), "Right Awareness", p. 108

quotes.text: Right Effort isn’t so much the effort to make the world a different place, as it is the effort to understand the nature of this world, of our body, our mind, this life.
quotes.author: Jack Kornfield
quotes.source: The Eightfold Path for the Householder (talks, 1995), "Right Effort", p. 65

quotes.text: If you really want to learn something in a full way — tennis, piano, not to speak of training the mind and opening the heart — it takes perseverance, patience and a systematic training.
quotes.author: Jack Kornfield
quotes.source: The Eightfold Path for the Householder (talks, 1995), "Right Understanding", p. 11

quotes.text: We don’t need more oil and food as much as we need somebody who understands how to avoid getting caught in anger and fear and prejudice. And that somebody is you.
quotes.author: Jack Kornfield
quotes.source: The Eightfold Path for the Householder (talks, 1995), "Right Understanding", p. 7

quotes.text: While we might think of love as a feeling, we can also think of it as an ability.
quotes.author: Sharon Salzberg
quotes.source: Real Love: The Art of Mindful Connection, as discussed in "The Power of Real Love," Lion's Roar, Nov 4, 2017

quotes.text: I think love and joy come from the same place—the ability to be with what is happening with an open heart and mind.
quotes.author: Sharon Salzberg
quotes.source: Real Love: The Art of Mindful Connection

quotes.text: The key in letting go is practice. Each time we let go, we disentangle ourselves from our expectations and begin to experience things as they are.
quotes.author: Sharon Salzberg
quotes.source: Real Love: The Art of Mindful Connection

quotes.text: The more we practice sympathetic joy, the more we come to realize that the happiness we share with others is inseparable from our own happiness.
quotes.author: Sharon Salzberg
quotes.source: Real Love: The Art of Mindful Connection

quotes.text: You might still feel rage, desire, and shame like everyone else in the world, but you can learn to hold these emotions in a context of caring.
quotes.author: Sharon Salzberg
quotes.source: Real Love: The Art of Mindful Connection

quotes.text: If you still find yourself caught up in self-criticism, turn your attention to the mere fact that you have an urge toward happiness. There is kindness and beauty in that.
quotes.author: Sharon Salzberg
quotes.source: Real Love: The Art of Mindful Connection

quotes.text: The way to get from point A to point B is really to be at A.
quotes.author: Larry Rosenberg
quotes.source: Breath by Breath: The Liberating Practice of Insight Meditation (Shambhala, 1998); excerpted in Tricycle, Spring 1998

quotes.text: In a Buddhist monastery, monks treat the guideline of not taking what is not given with utmost seriousness. Monks do not take the razor, book, robe, or begging bowl of another monk without securing permission first. It is a discipline in letting go, in patience, and in waiting for something to be available.
quotes.author: Christopher Titmuss
quotes.source: Light on Enlightenment (Rider/Shambhala, 2000)

quotes.text: A compassionate life is a fearless life.
quotes.author: Christina Feldman
quotes.source: Boundless Heart: The Buddha's Path of Kindness, Compassion, Joy, and Equanimity (Shambhala, 2017)

quotes.text: Relinquishment is letting go of everything that is not authentic and natural.
quotes.author: Rodney Smith
quotes.source: Stepping Out of Self-Deception: The Buddha's Liberating Teaching of No-Self (Shambhala, 2010)

quotes.text: Learning to pause is the first step in the practice of Radical Acceptance.
quotes.author: Tara Brach
quotes.source: Radical Acceptance: Embracing Your Life with the Heart of a Buddha (Bantam, 2003)

quotes.text: It's a big step, of course, from freeways to famines to wars, but it's wonderful to have confirmation that spacious acceptance is humanly possible. Spiritual practice might be discovering that potential in ourselves and enlarging it.
quotes.author: Sylvia Boorstein
quotes.source: It's Easier Than You Think: The Buddhist Way to Happiness (HarperOne, 1995)

quotes.text: The secret to skillful meditation is bringing your attention back with great patience and kindness.
quotes.author: James Baraz
quotes.source: "Mindfulness: The Most Direct Path," Lion's Roar, September 1, 2010

quotes.text: Racism is a heart disease. How we think and respond is at the core of racial suffering and racial healing. If we cannot think clearly and respond wisely, we will continue to damage the world's heart.
quotes.author: Ruth King
quotes.source: Mindful of Race: Transforming Racism from the Inside Out (Sounds True, 2018)

quotes.text: When we're purifying ourselves, when we're letting go of ancestral sorrows, it doesn't necessarily come with bliss and light.
quotes.author: Spring Washam
quotes.source: A Fierce Heart: Finding Strength, Courage, and Wisdom in Any Moment (Hay House, 2017); excerpted in Kosmos Journal

quotes.text: You can dramatically extend life—not by multiplying the number of your years, but by expanding the fullness of your moments.
quotes.author: Shinzen Young
quotes.source: The Science of Enlightenment: How Meditation Works, Ch. 1 (Sounds True, 2016)

quotes.text: You can choose any time of the day to step off the train of thought and into awake awareness. Once you've done this, you will naturally find new motivation, creativity, kindness, and passion for life.
quotes.author: Loch Kelly
quotes.source: Shift into Freedom: The Science and Practice of Open-Hearted Awareness (Sounds True, 2015)

quotes.text: The point is not to get rid of anger, nor to harbor ill will, but to own it, to pay attention to it patiently when it arises.
quotes.author: Taigen Dan Leighton
quotes.source: "A Kind of Performance Art," interview in Inquiring Mind, Vol. 28 No. 1, Fall 2011

quotes.text: Beyond any hurt, beyond any deed, this big forgiveness pervades all.
quotes.author: Norman Fischer
quotes.source: Sailing Home: Using the Wisdom of Homer's Odyssey to Navigate Life's Perils and Pitfalls

quotes.text: Attention or awareness is the secret of life and the heart of practice.
quotes.author: Charlotte Joko Beck
quotes.source: Nothing Special: Living Zen, excerpted as "Attention Means Attention," Tricycle, Fall 1993

quotes.text: If you cut off all thinking and keep this mind, 'How can I help?' the correct action will appear. That is great love, great compassion, and great bodhisattva way.
quotes.author: Seung Sahn
quotes.source: Only Don't Know: Selected Teaching Letters of Zen Master Seung Sahn

quotes.text: When settled on the breath, the heart becomes clear, peaceful, and still. Then, like a mountain pool, the heart begins to reflect all that is around it.
quotes.author: Gil Fronsdal
quotes.source: "How Mindfulness Works When Not Working," talk adapted for the Insight Meditation Center, Jan 1, 2001

quotes.text: When attention is impaired, it detracts from everything we do, and when it is well focused, it enhances everything we do.
quotes.author: B. Alan Wallace
quotes.source: The Attention Revolution: Unlocking the Power of the Focused Mind, Preface

quotes.text: I think the best definition, according to the Buddhist view, is that well-being is not just a mere pleasurable sensation. It is a deep sense of serenity and fulfillment.
quotes.author: Matthieu Ricard
quotes.source: "The Habits of Happiness," TED2004

quotes.text: See that thoughts of fear neither come nor go. See that thoughts of fear neither arise nor cease. Then look at the essence beyond coming and going, beyond arising and ceasing; look at this essence and let go and relax.
quotes.author: Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche
quotes.source: "See the True Nature, then Let Go and Relax in That," interview with Melvin McLeod, Buddhadharma, 2004, trans. Ari Goldfield

quotes.text: Knowing others is intelligence; knowing yourself is true wisdom.
quotes.author: Lao Tzu
quotes.source: Tao Te Ching, Verse 33, trans. Stephen Mitchell (Harper Perennial, 1988)

quotes.text: The struggle itself toward the heights is enough to fill a man's heart. One must imagine Sisyphus happy.
quotes.author: Albert Camus
quotes.source: The Myth of Sisyphus, trans. Justin O'Brien (Alfred A. Knopf, 1955)

quotes.text: Mind creates the abyss, the heart crosses it.
quotes.author: Nisargadatta Maharaj
quotes.source: I Am That, Ch. 3, trans. Maurice Frydman (Chetana, 1973)

quotes.text: There is now little question that how one uses one's attention, moment to moment, largely determines what kind of person one becomes.
quotes.author: Sam Harris
quotes.source: Waking Up: A Guide to Spirituality Without Religion (2014)

quotes.text: Consciousness is simply the light by which the contours of mind and body are known.
quotes.author: Sam Harris
quotes.source: Waking Up: A Guide to Spirituality Without Religion (2014)

quotes.text: Why are we born? We are born so that we will not have to be born again.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: No Ajahn Chah: Reflections

quotes.text: You say that you are too busy to meditate. Do you have time to breathe? Meditation is your breath.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: No Ajahn Chah: Reflections

quotes.text: Only one book is worth reading: the heart.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: No Ajahn Chah: Reflections

quotes.text: The mind is intrinsically tranquil. Out of this tranquility, anxiety and confusion are born.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: No Ajahn Chah: Reflections

quotes.text: Death is as close as our breath.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: No Ajahn Chah: Reflections

quotes.text: If the body could talk, it would be telling us all day long, 'You're not my owner, you know.'
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: No Ajahn Chah: Reflections

quotes.text: A good practice is to ask yourself very sincerely, 'Why was I born?' Ask yourself this question in the morning, in the afternoon, and at night every day.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: No Ajahn Chah: Reflections

quotes.text: Our birth and death are just one thing. You can't have one without the other.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: No Ajahn Chah: Reflections

quotes.text: I'm always talking about things to develop and things to give up, but really there's nothing to develop and nothing to give up.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: No Ajahn Chah: Reflections

quotes.text: I live nowhere. There is no place you can find me. I have no age. To have age, you must exist, and to think you exist is already a problem.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: No Ajahn Chah: Reflections

quotes.text: With mindfulness you can see the real owner of things. Do you think this is your world, your body? It is the world's world, the body's body. We only rent this house. Why not find out who really owns it?
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Still Forest Pool

quotes.text: I know this glass is already broken, so I enjoy it incredibly.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Still Forest Pool

quotes.text: Yesterday is a memory. Tomorrow is the unknown. Now is the knowing.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Now Is the Knowing (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: Our practice is not to become enlightened, but to be in the knowing, now.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Now Is the Knowing (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: Although the conditions of the mind may not be peaceful at all, the mind itself is a peaceful place.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Now Is the Knowing (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: The realization of samsara is the condition of Nibbana. As we recognize the cycles of habit and are no longer deluded by them, we realize Nibbana.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Now Is the Knowing (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: The reality of now is magnificent and awesome.
quotes.author: Ajahn Brahm
quotes.source: Mindfulness, Bliss, and Beyond: A Meditator's Handbook

quotes.text: So if you seek truth, you should value silent awareness and consider it more important than any thought.
quotes.author: Ajahn Brahm
quotes.source: Mindfulness, Bliss, and Beyond: A Meditator's Handbook

quotes.text: When one realizes that most of our thinking is really pointless, that it gets us nowhere and only gives us headaches, we gladly and easily spend much time in inner quiet.
quotes.author: Ajahn Brahm
quotes.source: Mindfulness, Bliss, and Beyond: A Meditator's Handbook

quotes.text: The motto of meditation is no joy, no mindfulness.
quotes.author: Ajahn Brahm
quotes.source: Mindfulness, Bliss, and Beyond: A Meditator's Handbook

quotes.text: Silence is shy. If silence hears you talking about her, she vanishes immediately.
quotes.author: Ajahn Brahm
quotes.source: Mindfulness, Bliss, and Beyond: A Meditator's Handbook

quotes.text: Mindfulness brings to light experience in its pure immediacy. It reveals the object as it is before it has been plastered over with conceptual paint, overlaid with interpretations.
quotes.author: Bhikkhu Bodhi
quotes.source: The Noble Eightfold Path: The Way to the End of Suffering

quotes.text: The tool the Buddha holds out to free the mind from desire is understanding. Real renunciation is not a matter of compelling ourselves to give up things still inwardly cherished, but of changing our perspective on them so that they no longer bind us.
quotes.author: Bhikkhu Bodhi
quotes.source: The Noble Eightfold Path: The Way to the End of Suffering

quotes.text: Like a lake unruffled by any breeze, the concentrated mind is a faithful reflector that mirrors whatever is placed before it exactly as it is.
quotes.author: Bhikkhu Bodhi
quotes.source: The Noble Eightfold Path: The Way to the End of Suffering

quotes.text: Whatever you're doing, and especially when you don't seem to be doing anything at all, don't be complacent. Look carefully, again and again, for even the slightest stress or disturbance you might be causing inadvertently, and learn how to drop whatever you're doing that's causing it.
quotes.author: Thanissaro Bhikkhu
quotes.source: The Practice in a Word (in Purity of Heart)

quotes.text: Heedfulness is the path to the Deathless. Heedlessness is the path to death. The heedful die not. The heedless are as if dead already.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada, v. 21, trans. Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: All conditioned things are unsatisfactory. When one sees this with wisdom, one turns away from suffering.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada, v. 278, trans. Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Better than a thousand hollow words is one word that brings peace.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada, v. 100, trans. Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: The profound teaching is whatever you can't do yet. It's not something that's always intellectually difficult, but it's profound if you haven't yet penetrated it.
quotes.author: Ajahn Jayasaro
quotes.source: Reflections (Abhayagiri Monastery)

quotes.text: The blossoming of compassion is seen as the measure of an awakening mind.
quotes.author: Ajahn Jayasaro
quotes.source: Without and Within: Questions and Answers on the Teachings of Theravāda Buddhism, question 75, "In Buddhism, how important is it to help others?"

quotes.text: Giving without expectations is empowering, reduces attachments and gives rise to self-respect and joy.
quotes.author: Ajahn Jayasaro
quotes.source: Without and Within: Questions and Answers on the Teachings of Theravāda Buddhism, question 95, "What determines the spiritual quality of giving?"

quotes.text: The most important thing is not to stop. As long as meditators keep putting effort into their meditation, come what may, they are accumulating the conditions for success.
quotes.author: Ajahn Jayasaro
quotes.source: Without and Within: Questions and Answers on the Teachings of Theravāda Buddhism, question 113, "What is the key to a successful long-term meditation practice?"

quotes.text: Constancy and regularity of practice are extremely helpful. Although meditation is not a race, the steady-paced tortoise mind will always have the advantage over the hare.
quotes.author: Ajahn Jayasaro
quotes.source: Without and Within: Questions and Answers on the Teachings of Theravāda Buddhism, question 113, "What is the key to a successful long-term meditation practice?"

quotes.text: The wish to make others happy or to relieve them of their suffering is a wonderful jewel of the human mind. But for noble feelings to lead to effective action, wisdom is needed.
quotes.author: Ajahn Jayasaro
quotes.source: Without and Within: Questions and Answers on the Teachings of Theravāda Buddhism, question 75, "In Buddhism, how important is it to help others?"

quotes.text: Chanda is the desire that arises from a correct understanding of the way things are. At its heart lies the aspiration for truth and goodness.
quotes.author: Ajahn Jayasaro
quotes.source: Without and Within: Questions and Answers on the Teachings of Theravāda Buddhism, question 22, "Is it correct that Buddhism teaches us to give up all desires?"

quotes.text: Every time we intentionally cause harm, the native kindness and sensitivity of the human heart is obscured.
quotes.author: Ajahn Munindo
quotes.source: In Any Given Moment, "Difficult Lessons"

quotes.text: Guilt is a distorted form of aversion and manifests as self-hatred, obscuring any possibility of real contentment.
quotes.author: Ajahn Munindo
quotes.source: In Any Given Moment, "Difficult Lessons"

quotes.text: We make the suffering happen; being honest and mindful about the process of causing suffering is what leads to the letting go.
quotes.author: Ajahn Munindo
quotes.source: In Any Given Moment, "Riding the Waves"

quotes.text: Without kindness, compassion and empathetic joy, so-called equanimity can be a form of cold-hearted indifference.
quotes.author: Ajahn Munindo
quotes.source: In Any Given Moment, "Contentment"

quotes.text: In reality there are no problems. In reality there are difficulties, pain and irritation, but problems are something extra we create out of the resistance which is an expression of unawareness.
quotes.author: Ajahn Munindo
quotes.source: In Any Given Moment, "Venerable Venerables"

quotes.text: If you notice that you are still entertaining attitudes of untamed greed in the way you hold your meditation, try dwelling on how you would hold a newborn baby – gently, softly and lovingly.
quotes.author: Ajahn Munindo
quotes.source: In Any Given Moment, "Sitting in the Buddha’s Waiting Room"

quotes.text: The truth of desire is that it is a movement in the mind. It is not who we are, though we readily make a sense of self out of it.
quotes.author: Ajahn Munindo
quotes.source: Alert to the Needs of the Journey, "Keep Moving On"

quotes.text: When we are suffering, the truth is that here and now we are imposing limitations on awareness. If we are honest we won’t blame others, we won’t blame the world.
quotes.author: Ajahn Munindo
quotes.source: Alert to the Needs of the Journey, "Keep Moving On"

quotes.text: Insight sees through the world, revealing its instability and the fruitlessness of our habits of clinging. Wisdom sees how the clinging creates resistance and causes suffering. The warm-hearted expression of such wisdom is compassion.
quotes.author: Ajahn Munindo
quotes.source: Alert to the Needs of the Journey, "Keep Moving On"

quotes.text: We stop struggling to change the nature of the world, and work instead on our relationship with the world.
quotes.author: Ajahn Munindo
quotes.source: Alert to the Needs of the Journey, "The Right Sort of Peace"

quotes.text: Wanting to give up doesn’t mean we have to give up.
quotes.author: Ajahn Munindo
quotes.source: Alert to the Needs of the Journey, "Keep Moving On"

quotes.text: By way of experiment, instead of struggling against some activity which is taking place in awareness, try attending to the quality of awareness itself, the just-knowing mind.
quotes.author: Ajahn Munindo
quotes.source: Alert to the Needs of the Journey, "The Right Sort of Peace"

quotes.text: A favourite reflection of mine is: “Infinite patience, boundless compassion.” This is the practice.
quotes.author: Ajahn Viradhammo
quotes.source: The Stillness of Being, "Bringing the Teachings Alive"

quotes.text: Attachment is very up and down but compassion is calm. It is not a demand that you make me happy.
quotes.author: Ajahn Viradhammo
quotes.source: The Stillness of Being, "Dhamma and Family Life"

quotes.text: Truthfulness is the heart of the religious life because enlightenment is about truth. Freedom is about truth and suffering is about ignorance, about not understanding.
quotes.author: Ajahn Viradhammo
quotes.source: The Stillness of Being, "Acceptance and Responsibility"

quotes.text: The happiness of a relatively calm mind is not complete freedom. This is still just another experience.
quotes.author: Ajahn Viradhammo
quotes.source: The Stillness of Being, "So What"

quotes.text: Even within a spiritual practice we can have a cruel self-hating attitude towards the very real difficulties that we face. We can demand that we be loving, or forgiving.
quotes.author: Ajahn Viradhammo
quotes.source: The Stillness of Being, "Affectionate Living"

quotes.text: An angry thought is not mine, it’s a condition of nature; it arises and ceases.
quotes.author: Ajahn Viradhammo
quotes.source: The Stillness of Being, "Bringing the Teachings Alive"

quotes.text: Sometimes it's better to be harmonious than to be right.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: The Ajahn Pasanno Question and Story Archive, Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery

quotes.text: The not-self refrain, 'This is not me, this is not mine, this is not what or who I am,' is not an abdication of responsibility but an understanding: this is the way I can put things down and move on.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: The Ajahn Pasanno Question and Story Archive, Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery

quotes.text: If you respond to somebody with anger and aversion, you’ll probably get a negative response back. If you respond with kindness and patience, you tend to get that same response back.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: Nourishing the Roots, "Purifying the Foundation"

quotes.text: Mindfulness is the ability to have balance, to not be pulled in, the willingness to relinquish or let go of the positions we tend to take.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: Nourishing the Roots, "Purifying the Foundation"

quotes.text: Ānāpānasati is a meditation that one can take wherever one goes. You have to breathe, so it’s always there for you, always present.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: Nourishing the Roots, "Mindfulness of Breathing: Food for the Heart"

quotes.text: The contemplation of change is a doorway to insight.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: Nourishing the Roots, "Mindfulness of Breathing: Food for the Heart"

quotes.text: We don’t need to be keeping precepts out of fear of divine retribution; it is an opportunity to beautify the heart and to create the conditions for increased refinement and clarity.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: Nourishing the Roots, "What Accords With Dhamma"

quotes.text: We want to abandon suffering, to let go of suffering, but when it isn’t known—when it isn’t understood clearly—then the cause is still simmering underneath.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: Nourishing the Roots, "Awakening Through the Noble Truths"

quotes.text: As the mind becomes settled, then there’s a reflection and acknowledgment, an understanding: “Oh. Mindfulness is present, and I am content.”
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: Beneath the Bodhi Tree, "Balancing the Mind"

quotes.text: The nature of desire is that it’s always going to feel like it’s not enough.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: Beneath the Bodhi Tree, "Enjoying the Breath"

quotes.text: When we’re faced with suffering or difficulty, or stress, discontent, dissatisfaction, the habit, culturally, is to seek some kind of pleasure as an escape or distraction.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: Beneath the Bodhi Tree, "Beneath the Bodhi Tree"

quotes.text: Relinquishing attachment has to rely on something more than just having the right idea, thought, concept, or view.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: Beneath the Bodhi Tree, "Beneath the Bodhi Tree"

quotes.text: You start realizing it’s not a path of attainment but of relinquishing.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: Beneath the Bodhi Tree, "Gradual Instruction"

quotes.text: Dāna is not just something one is doing through material things: it’s that quality of heart that is ready to give, to share, to help, to be of benefit.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: Beneath the Bodhi Tree, "Gradual Instruction"

quotes.text: Recognizing the power of mindfulness is wisdom in and of itself. The sustaining, cherishing, willingness to maintain the quality of mindfulness takes relinquishment. It takes letting go.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: On Becoming and Stopping (Dhamma talk)

quotes.text: We know how to become but we don’t know how to stop. We’re not used to stopping.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: On Becoming and Stopping (Dhamma talk)

quotes.text: Each moment of mindfulness is the opportunity to verify the Dhamma of the Buddha.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: On Becoming and Stopping (Dhamma talk)

quotes.text: Trying to replace desire and greed with trying hard to become perfect practitioners is fraught with suffering.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: On Becoming and Stopping (Dhamma talk)

quotes.text: Becoming is why we continually opt to be scattered, confused and stupid rather than peaceful and wise.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: On Becoming and Stopping (Dhamma talk)

quotes.text: You will see that if you actually stop and stand in awareness, you’ll be able to accomplish things a lot more skillfully.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: On Becoming and Stopping (Dhamma talk)

quotes.text: When the end of suffering (Nibbāna) is the topic, one would think the writing about it would be less suffering. Curious how some things are not as they appear.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: The Island: An Anthology of the Buddha's Teachings on Nibbāna, p. 8 (Ajahn Pasanno's preface)

quotes.text: If there is any hint of self, a position is then taken and the whole realm of saṃsāra unfolds.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno
quotes.source: The Island: An Anthology of the Buddha's Teachings on Nibbāna, p. 8 (Ajahn Pasanno's preface)

quotes.text: True insight practice is awareness of all of the mental and physical phenomena that are constantly arising at the six sense-doors.
quotes.author: Mahasi Sayadaw
quotes.source: Manual of Insight
