quotes.text: When conventional reality emerges, ultimate reality submerges. When ultimate reality emerges, conventional reality submerges.
quotes.author: Mahasi Sayadaw
quotes.source: Manual of Insight

quotes.text: During meditation you become someone who has no history.
quotes.author: Ajahn Brahm
quotes.source: Mindfulness, Bliss, and Beyond: A Meditator's Handbook

quotes.text: You do not do anything. If you try to do something at this stage, you will disturb the whole process. The beauty will be lost.
quotes.author: Ajahn Brahm
quotes.source: Mindfulness, Bliss, and Beyond: A Meditator's Handbook

quotes.text: Just try to keep your mind in the present. Whatever arises in the mind, just watch it and let go of it. Don't even wish to be rid of thoughts. Then the mind will return to its natural state.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Still Forest Pool

quotes.text: If we see everything as uncertain, then their value fades away.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Still Forest Pool / No Ajahn Chah

quotes.text: Have you ever seen still, flowing water? There. Right where your thinking cannot take you.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Still, Flowing Water

quotes.text: The Dhamma is just like this, talking in similes, because the Dhamma doesn't have anything. It isn't round, doesn't have any corners.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: In Simple Terms

quotes.text: Your external home is not your real home. It is your supposed home, your home in the world. As for your real home, that's peace.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: In Simple Terms

quotes.text: We turn towards the Dhamma, we are aware now, take refuge in Dhamma, now as an immediate action, an immediate reflection of being the Dhamma.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Now Is the Knowing (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: When we no longer identify with the sensory world as me or mine, and see it as anatta, we can enjoy the senses without seeking sense-impingement or depending on it.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Now Is the Knowing (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: This is our practice of letting go. We let go of our identification with conditions by seeing that they are all impermanent and not-self.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Now Is the Knowing (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: The whole aim of our practice is purity of heart. Everything else is just games.
quotes.author: Ajahn Fuang
quotes.source: As quoted by Thanissaro Bhikkhu in Purity of Heart, opening section (dhammatalks.org)

quotes.text: Purity of heart is a happiness that will never harm anyone.
quotes.author: Thanissaro Bhikkhu
quotes.source: Purity of Heart

quotes.text: If a person isn't true to the Buddha's teachings, the Buddha's teachings won't be true to that person, and that person won't be able to know what the Buddha's true teachings are.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: As quoted by Thanissaro Bhikkhu in The Customs of the Noble Ones (1999, accesstoinsight.org)

quotes.text: The mind can train itself to abandon unskillful qualities and to develop skillful qualities in their place.
quotes.author: Thanissaro Bhikkhu
quotes.source: The Buddha's Teachings (dhammatalks.org)

quotes.text: Heedfulness, in turn, has to be paired with an attitude that is not easily contented with the results you're getting from your actions.
quotes.author: Thanissaro Bhikkhu
quotes.source: The Buddha's Teachings (dhammatalks.org)

quotes.text: You begin to enjoy the silence, once you have found it at last, and that is why it grows.
quotes.author: Ajahn Brahm
quotes.source: Mindfulness, Bliss, and Beyond: A Meditator's Handbook

quotes.text: In that silent awareness of just now you will experience much peace, joy and consequent wisdom.
quotes.author: Ajahn Brahm
quotes.source: Mindfulness, Bliss, and Beyond: A Meditator's Handbook

quotes.text: About this mind, in truth there is nothing really wrong with it. It is intrinsically pure. Within itself it's already peaceful.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Food for the Heart

quotes.text: If things seem to be good, don't delight in them, and if they're not good don't be averse to them. Just look at it all. Just look, don't bother judging.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Food for the Heart

quotes.text: Good and bad can both bite, so don't hold fast to them.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Food for the Heart

quotes.text: When you listen to the Dhamma, you must open up your heart and compose yourself in its centre. Don't try and accumulate what you hear.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: The Teachings of Ajahn Chah

quotes.text: To define Buddhism without a lot of words and phrases, we can simply say, don't cling or hold on to anything. Harmonize with actuality, with things just as they are.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: The Teachings of Ajahn Chah

quotes.text: Practice is not moving forward, but there is forward movement. At the same time, it is not moving back, but there is backward movement.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: The Teachings of Ajahn Chah

quotes.text: Paccattam veditabbo vinnuhi. The wise must know for themselves.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Food for the Heart

quotes.text: If you wonder, is this wrong or not, that is, you're not really sure, then don't say it, don't act on it, don't discard your restraint.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Food for the Heart

quotes.text: If there is no mutual respect, negligence sets in and the practice eventually degenerates.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Food for the Heart

quotes.text: One who wishes to reach the Buddha-Dhamma must be one who has faith or confidence as a foundation.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Bodhinyana

quotes.text: Buddha is the one who knows, the one who has purity, radiance and peace in the heart.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Bodhinyana

quotes.text: Wisdom does not come from studying great theories and philosophies, but from observing the ordinary.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Teachings from the Forest

quotes.text: We tend to overlook the ordinary. For example, we are usually only aware of our breath when it's abnormal.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Teachings from the Forest

quotes.text: Anicca, dukkha and anatta are not concepts we believe in, but things we can observe.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Teachings from the Forest

quotes.text: Most meditation is just allowing anything that has arisen to cease. That's why I stress patience: allow things to take their natural course to cessation.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Teachings from the Forest

quotes.text: Try to accept even the things you don't like about yourself. Don't try to be too perfect.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Teachings from the Forest

quotes.text: You always have this patient-kindness and peaceful coexistence with whatever comes.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Teachings from the Forest

quotes.text: The knower is always now. We don't know about the past or future. Knowing now is the Buddha-knowing.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Teachings from the Forest

quotes.text: Change never has any fixed point, except that you can know change.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Teachings from the Forest

quotes.text: Every condition must change. If you like the condition then you will feel sorrow, despair, loss. When an unpleasant condition goes, then you feel glad.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Teachings from the Forest

quotes.text: You can abide in emptiness by just standing among the barren trees of winter and looking at them without creating anything onto them. One can feel a sense of perfect calm and contentment with just being still and silent like the trees.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: The Way It Is, "Stillness and Response" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: Sickness, and old age and death is something we can always bear with. That's not real suffering. But the suffering is the greed, hatred and delusion we produce through the self-view, through taking it all personally.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: The Way It Is, "The Formations of Self" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: Letting go means to be able to be with what is displeasing without dwelling in aversion - because aversion is an attachment.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: The Way It Is, "Letting Go of Desire" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: The stillness and silence is ever-present wherever we are, no matter what condition we happen to be in.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: The Way It Is, "Stillness and Response" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: You do not become a vacuous zombie through understanding Dhamma. You still relate to each other but it is through kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy and serenity, rather than through greed hatred and delusion.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: The Way It Is, "Letting Go of Desire" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: The practice of meditation is reflecting on 'the way it is' in order to see the fears and desires which we create. This is quite a simple practice, but the practice of Dhamma should be very very simple rather than complicated.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: The Way It Is, "The Way It Is" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: Conditions are extraordinary, but the peace of the mind, the unconditioned, is so ordinary that nobody ever notices it.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Now Is the Knowing, "Anapanasati" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: Without evaluating or analyzing, when we simply recognize thought as thought it begins to slow down and stop. This isn’t annihilation; this is allowing things to cease. It is compassion.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Now Is the Knowing, "Anapanasati" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: Once we are aware that we have wandered off the breath, then we very gently return to it. We use the attitude of being very, very patient and always willing to begin again.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Now Is the Knowing, "Anapanasati" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: Most people like the idea of peace, but find the actual experience of it disappointing or frustrating. They desire stimulation, something that will draw them into itself.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Now Is the Knowing, "Anapanasati" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: Meditation is a way of cleaning the window, purifying the mind, allowing things to come up into consciousness and letting them go.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Now Is the Knowing, "Happiness, Unhappiness and Nibbana" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: Sometimes we get too serious about everything, totally lacking in joy and happiness, with no sense of humour, just repressing everything. Gladden the mind, put a smile on your dial!
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Now Is the Knowing, "Anapanasati" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: If I am thinking, ‘I’ve got to be mindful’ while I am being mindful, I can see and be aware that I have this idea, ‘I’ve got to be mindful’. That’s mindfulness.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Teachings from the Forest, "Nothing Is More Joyless than Selfishness" (Amaravati Publications, 2025)

quotes.text: Being sensitive to the needs and the type of people we are with, the time and the place, and the kind of culture we are in – all of this is part of our practice of being mindful.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Teachings from the Forest, "Nothing Is More Joyless than Selfishness" (Amaravati Publications, 2025)

quotes.text: Desire is energy that’s always looking for something or another.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Teachings from the Forest, "Everything Around Us Is Dhamma" (Amaravati Publications, 2025)

quotes.text: We let desire be. It’s not a matter of getting rid of desire, but of letting it cease.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Teachings from the Forest, "Everything Around Us Is Dhamma" (Amaravati Publications, 2025)

quotes.text: When there is love, that is not a personal thing; even though it seems personal, it’s a condition. Love that is present in my mind is the same kind of thing that is present in yours.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Teachings from the Forest, "The Three Characteristics" (Amaravati Publications, 2025)

quotes.text: Wisdom also allows us to wonder again, to be open to the unknown and not frightened by it anymore, allowing this conditioned self we carry through ignorance to cease in the mind.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Teachings from the Forest, "Innocence Is Corruptible; Wisdom Is Incorruptible" (Amaravati Publications, 2025)

quotes.text: To be mindful means to have mettā towards the fear in your mind, or the anger, or the jealousy.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Mindfulness: The Path to the Deathless, "Kindness" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: The obstacle to concentration practice is aversion to failure and the incredible desire to succeed. Practice is not a matter of will-power, but of wisdom, of noting wisdom.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Mindfulness: The Path to the Deathless, "The Mantra Buddho" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: What arises passes, and in its passing is peace.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Mindfulness: The Path to the Deathless, "The Need for Wisdom in the World" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: Much of the lesson in life is learning to endure what we don’t like in ourselves and in the world around us; being able to be patient and kindly, and not make a scene over the imperfections in the sensory experience.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Mindfulness: The Path to the Deathless, "What is Meditation" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: Develop a normal pace, because our meditation moves around the ordinary things rather than the special.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Mindfulness: The Path to the Deathless, "Mindfulness of the Ordinary" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: Just relax and don’t make meditation into a burdensome task for yourself. See it as an opportunity to be peaceful and at ease with the moment.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: Mindfulness: The Path to the Deathless, "Effort and Relaxation" (Amaravati Publications)

quotes.text: It takes much less skill to live with mosquitoes than with another person.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: It's Like This: Ninety Reflections to Honour Luang Por Sumedho in His Ninetieth Year, No. 7 (Amaravati Publications, 2024)

quotes.text: What’s left when there is no grasping is consciousness knowing itself, awareness aware of awareness.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: It's Like This: Ninety Reflections to Honour Luang Por Sumedho in His Ninetieth Year, No. 28 (Amaravati Publications, 2024)

quotes.text: Paññā, or wisdom, comes from intuition, not from analysis. You can know all about Buddhism and still not use any wisdom in your life.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: It's Like This: Ninety Reflections to Honour Luang Por Sumedho in His Ninetieth Year, No. 47 (Amaravati Publications, 2024)

quotes.text: Enlightenment is nothing more than growing up, being a mature human being.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: It's Like This: Ninety Reflections to Honour Luang Por Sumedho in His Ninetieth Year, No. 82 (Amaravati Publications, 2024)

quotes.text: Conviviality is an attitude of being at ease with life, of openness and ease with being alive and breathing, at ease with being present with what is arising in consciousness.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: It's Like This: Ninety Reflections to Honour Luang Por Sumedho in His Ninetieth Year, No. 73 (Amaravati Publications, 2024)

quotes.text: Keep the practice simple: live your life mindfully and morally, and have faith in letting go.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sumedho
quotes.source: It's Like This: Ninety Reflections to Honour Luang Por Sumedho in His Ninetieth Year, No. 42 (Amaravati Publications, 2024)

quotes.text: Desire is a liar.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Just One More, Appreciative Joy, pp. 20-22, quoted in Abhayagiri Reflections, "Desire Is a Liar" (13 Jan. 2017)

quotes.text: All symbols and similes are partially relevant. All analogies are partial.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Quoted in Abhayagiri teachings

quotes.text: Whether we experience pleasure or pain, success or failure, praise or criticism, that knowing nature of the mind is utterly serene.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Small Boat, Great Mountain: Theravadan Reflections on the Natural Great Perfection, Ch. 3, "The View from the Forest"

quotes.text: We practice to end suffering, yet we get so attached to working with things in the mind that when the dukkha stops and the heart becomes spacious and empty, we can find ourselves feeling lost.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Small Boat, Great Mountain: Theravadan Reflections on the Natural Great Perfection, Ch. 3, "The View from the Forest"

quotes.text: We need to see that the heart is attached somewhere and then make the gesture to loosen up, to let go. Sometimes we don’t notice where the suffering gets generated.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Small Boat, Great Mountain: Theravadan Reflections on the Natural Great Perfection, Ch. 1, "Ultimate and Conventional Reality"

quotes.text: Movement does not apply to awareness. There are movements of the body, but the mind that knows the movements aren’t moving. There’s stillness, but there’s flow.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Small Boat, Great Mountain: Theravadan Reflections on the Natural Great Perfection, Ch. 2, "The Place of Nonabiding"

quotes.text: Wisdom can develop only in a mind that is continually reoriented and grounded in truth and selflessness.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Small Boat, Great Mountain: Theravadan Reflections on the Natural Great Perfection, Ch. 8, "The Portable Retreat"

quotes.text: We can talk about things like knowing, emptiness, lucidity, clarity, and so forth, but when the mind is fully awake to its own nature, the words run out.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Small Boat, Great Mountain: Theravadan Reflections on the Natural Great Perfection, Ch. 7, "Off the Wheel"

quotes.text: Until we know the pain of attachment, we won’t really let go.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Who Is Pulling the Strings?, "Questions and Answers"

quotes.text: The world is definitely pre-conditioned but what we do with it here in the present moment is entirely up to us.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Who Is Pulling the Strings?, "Is This Principle of ‘Karmic Fate’ What the Buddha Taught?"

quotes.text: Moment by moment we are not experiencing an objective world; rather we’re experiencing our mind’s representation of the world.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Who Is Pulling the Strings?, "Is This a Conscious Universe?"

quotes.text: The cause of death is birth. Death is going to happen to all of us in some way or other, everyone is going to die.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Who Is Pulling the Strings?, "Questions and Answers"

quotes.text: A lot of our suffering, of dukkha, comes from a feeling of dissatisfaction or discontent because we think: ‘It shouldn’t be this way,’ ‘Life is unfair,’ ‘Why is this happening to me?’ or ‘Not this again – I don’t deserve this!’
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Who Is Pulling the Strings?, "Is Nature Fair?"

quotes.text: To me, then, evil is not something outside of nature, but I would say that it entails a depth of delusion whereby the mind is completely lost in its own self-obsessions.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Who Is Pulling the Strings?, "Questions and Answers"

quotes.text: Happiness is a fickle friend, no more than freedom from midges; freedom from suffering is another story.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Tudong: The Long Road North, Part 3

quotes.text: Walking in the world you are bound to do some damage, however hard you try to be gentle. Our reflection though is that we walk for peace; at least we are not starting any wars.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Tudong: The Long Road North, Part 3

quotes.text: Negativity and the situations you blame for your suffering always seem to find a way of dissolving if you are patient.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Tudong: The Long Road North, Part 4

quotes.text: Letting go, renunciation of conventions, is the learning to be at ease in boundless emptiness.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Tudong: The Long Road North, Part 2

quotes.text: Finding true happiness in the world is an art, not a sin.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Tudong: The Long Road North, Part 4

quotes.text: As long as you are going somewhere you are living in the desire to get there and the fear of not making it: you feel a twinge in your knee, your arm goes dead, your shoe begins to rub; EEEEEEEEEEK! goes the mind.
quotes.author: Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: Tudong: The Long Road North, Part 1

quotes.text: When the heart is free of all obscurations, and is utterly in accord with nature, Ultimate Reality (Dhamma), it experiences perfect peace, joy and contentment.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: The Island: An Anthology of the Buddha's Teachings on Nibbāna, p. 28

quotes.text: The heart can be aware but to try to make awareness an object, in the same way that we would a tree or a thought, is a frustrating process.
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: The Island: An Anthology of the Buddha's Teachings on Nibbāna, p. 197

quotes.text: When there is insufficient mindfulness and wisdom, the mind ‘goes out’ and attaches to its perceptions and moods, the result of which is the experience of ‘me being pressured by life.’
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: The Island: An Anthology of the Buddha's Teachings on Nibbāna, p. 124

quotes.text: Because our sense impressions are so dependent on our sense organs, the sense of the world ‘out there’ as opposed to our self ‘in here’ does not accord with direct experience. When we see how this false dichotomy causes suffering, we will drop it and be released from our attachment both to ‘self’ and to ‘world.’
quotes.author: Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro
quotes.source: The Island: An Anthology of the Buddha's Teachings on Nibbāna, p. 259

quotes.text: In the seen, there is only the seen, in the heard, there is only the heard, in the sensed only the sensed, in the cognized only the cognized.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Bahiya Sutta (Ud 1.10), as quoted by Ajahn Amaro

quotes.text: Nothing whatsoever should be clung to.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Cula-tanha-sankhaya Sutta (MN 37), as quoted by Ajahn Amaro

quotes.text: When they do not cling, they are not agitated. When they are not agitated, they personally attain Nibbana.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Cula-tanha-sankhaya Sutta (MN 37)

quotes.text: The present moment is here to be used. It's not here just to hang out with the idea that this is what it's all about.
quotes.author: Thanissaro Bhikkhu
quotes.source: Talks and essays (dhammatalks.org)

quotes.text: What does it mean to be mindful of the breath? Something very simple: to keep the breath in mind.
quotes.author: Thanissaro Bhikkhu
quotes.source: Mindfulness Defined

quotes.text: Keep remembering the breath each time you breathe in, each time you breathe out.
quotes.author: Thanissaro Bhikkhu
quotes.source: Mindfulness Defined

quotes.text: We don't wish for suffering, but once we understand how to be in relationship with it, it becomes the means through which we mature as loving and wise people.
quotes.author: Thanissaro Bhikkhu
quotes.source: Various essays

quotes.text: The role that kamma plays in the awakening is empowering. It means that what each of us does, says, and thinks does matter.
quotes.author: Thanissaro Bhikkhu
quotes.source: The Meaning of the Buddha's Awakening (accesstoinsight.org); also in Refuge: An Introduction to the Buddha, Dhamma & Sangha

quotes.text: The choices we make in each moment of our lives are real, and they produce real consequences.
quotes.author: Thanissaro Bhikkhu
quotes.source: The Meaning of the Buddha's Awakening (accesstoinsight.org); also in Refuge: An Introduction to the Buddha, Dhamma & Sangha

quotes.text: Whoever develops mindfulness of death, thinking, O that I might live for the interval that it takes to breathe out after breathing in, that I might attend to the Blessed One's instructions, they are said to dwell heedfully.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Anguttara Nikaya, as translated by Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Long life can't be gotten with wealth, nor aging warded off with treasure. The wise say this life is next to nothing, impermanent, subject to change.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Various suttas, as translated by Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: The rich and the poor touch the touch of Death.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Various suttas, as translated by Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: When the perception of impermanence is developed and cultivated it eliminates all desire for sensual pleasures, for rebirth in the realm of luminous form, and for rebirth in a future life.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Samyutta Nikaya

quotes.text: Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the ending of form.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Samyutta Nikaya

quotes.text: All consciousness, past, future, or present, internal or external, solid or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near: all consciousness with right understanding: This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Samyutta Nikaya

quotes.text: There is no form at all that's permanent, everlasting, eternal, imperishable, and will last forever and ever.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Samyutta Nikaya

quotes.text: All composed things are like a dream, a phantom, a drop of dew, a flash of lightning. That is how to meditate on them, that is how to observe them.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Diamond Sutra, §32, trans. Thich Nhat Hanh, The Diamond That Cuts Through Illusion

quotes.text: Someone who looks for me in form or seeks me in sound is on a mistaken path and cannot see the Tathagata.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Diamond Sutra, §26, trans. Thich Nhat Hanh, The Diamond That Cuts Through Illusion

quotes.text: Subhuti, the past mind cannot be grasped, neither can the present mind or the future mind.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Diamond Sutra, §18, trans. Thich Nhat Hanh, The Diamond That Cuts Through Illusion

quotes.text: Subhuti, a bodhisattva who still depends on notions to practice generosity is like someone walking in the dark.
quotes.author: The Buddha
quotes.source: Diamond Sutra, §14, trans. Thich Nhat Hanh, The Diamond That Cuts Through Illusion

quotes.text: The streams, lakes, and rivers that flow down to the ocean, when they reach the ocean, all have the same blue color, the same salty taste.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: In Simple Terms

quotes.text: The same with human beings: it doesn't matter where they're from. When they reach the stream of the Dhamma, it's all the same Dhamma.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: In Simple Terms

quotes.text: Don't think that the Dhamma lies far away from you. It lies right with you. It's about you.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: In Simple Terms

quotes.text: The Dhamma is revealing itself in every moment, but only when the mind is quiet can we understand what it is saying.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Tree in a Forest

quotes.text: We are like maggots. Life is like a falling leaf. Our mind is like rain water.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Tree in a Forest

quotes.text: All the teachings are merely similes and comparisons, means to help the mind see the truth.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Tree in a Forest

quotes.text: If we establish the Buddha within our mind, then we see everything, we contemplate everything, as no different from ourselves.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Tree in a Forest

quotes.text: I am like a tree in a forest. Birds come to the tree, they sit on its branches and eat its fruits. To the birds, the fruit may be sweet or sour. From the tree's point of view, this is just the chattering of birds.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: No Ajahn Chah / various

quotes.text: Can you endure it?
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Various talks (often first response to suffering)

quotes.text: The way beyond suffering is neither to run away from it, wallow in it or even grit one's teeth and get through on will alone. The encouragement of patient endurance is to hold steady in the midst of difficulty.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Various talks

quotes.text: The abandonment of these three is synonymous with stream entry, the first level of enlightenment.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Food for the Heart

quotes.text: Dhamma is that which can cut through the problems and difficulties of mankind, gradually reducing them to nothing.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Bodhinyana

quotes.text: We can’t just let go by an act of will. It takes wisdom. Wisdom and the insight into impermanence. Only then can we start to drop things.
quotes.author: Ajahn Nyaniko
quotes.source: Talk: Dhamma-Vinaya is the priority. 26-07-2026

quotes.text: Our problem is that we like good results but don't like creating good causes.
quotes.author: Ajahn Khamdee Pabhaso
quotes.source: Making the Dhamma Your Own, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu
quotes.comment: Buddhist additions verified against the linked texts, 2 October 2026. Sources distinguish canonical verses, modern teachings, and recollections. Verse line breaks are collapsed to spaces; leading ellipses mark excerpts.

quotes.text: Mindfulness and discernment are the factors that govern the heart.
quotes.author: Ajahn Khamdee Pabhaso
quotes.source: Making the Dhamma Your Own, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Metta is indeed a universal, unselfish and all-embracing love.
quotes.author: Acharya Buddharakkhita
quotes.source: Metta: The Philosophy and Practice of Universal Love, §1, Introduction

quotes.text: True metta is devoid of self-interest.
quotes.author: Acharya Buddharakkhita
quotes.source: Metta: The Philosophy and Practice of Universal Love, §1, Introduction

quotes.text: Contentment is a characteristic of the really happy individual.
quotes.author: Piyadassi Thera
quotes.source: The Seven Factors of Enlightenment, §§IV–V (Wheel No. 1)

quotes.text: Calmness is not weakness.
quotes.author: Piyadassi Thera
quotes.source: The Seven Factors of Enlightenment, §§IV–V (Wheel No. 1)

quotes.text: Meditate on the word 'Buddho.'
quotes.author: Ajahn Sao Kantasilo
quotes.source: Ajaan Sao's Teaching, recollections by Ajahn Phut Thaniyo, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: You have to make it know inside.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sao Kantasilo
quotes.source: Ajaan Sao's Teaching, recollections by Ajahn Phut Thaniyo, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: You have to be mindful of the present and alert to the present, too.
quotes.author: Ajahn Suwat Suvaco
quotes.source: Right Concentration, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: You have to depend on both mindfulness and alertness together.
quotes.author: Ajahn Suwat Suvaco
quotes.source: Right Concentration, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Practice right at the mind.
quotes.author: Ajahn Dune Atulo
quotes.source: Gifts He Left Behind, §§30, 43, compiled by Phra Bodhinandamuni, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Not worrying, not being attached: That's the mental dwelling of those who practice.
quotes.author: Ajahn Dune Atulo
quotes.source: Gifts He Left Behind, §§30, 43, compiled by Phra Bodhinandamuni, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: However, diligence and heedfulness will eventually win for one the fruits of tranquillity.
quotes.author: Bhikkhu Khantipalo
quotes.source: Practical Advice for Meditators, Introduction / Regular Daily Sitting (Wheel Nos. 116–117)

quotes.text: For success, great persistence and evenness of effort are necessary.
quotes.author: Bhikkhu Khantipalo
quotes.source: Practical Advice for Meditators, Introduction / Regular Daily Sitting (Wheel Nos. 116–117)

quotes.text: For progress in Vipassana Meditation, a student must keep knowing Anicca as continuously as possible.
quotes.author: Sayagyi U Ba Khin
quotes.source: The Essentials of Buddha Dhamma in Meditative Practice, opening section (Wheel No. 231)

quotes.text: But the only safe remedy is to face it — with mindfulness.
quotes.author: Nyanaponika Thera
quotes.source: The Power of Mindfulness, §1, Tidying Up the Mental Household (Wheel Nos. 121–122)

quotes.text: … the difficulty is only the persistence in applying it.
quotes.author: Nyanaponika Thera
quotes.source: The Power of Mindfulness, §1, Tidying Up the Mental Household (Wheel Nos. 121–122)

quotes.text: … one should be aware of the feelings as a conditioned and transient process.
quotes.author: Nyanaponika Thera
quotes.source: Contemplation of Feeling, Introduction (Wheel Nos. 303–304)

quotes.text: We need to take a step back and be a neutral observer of the whole process.
quotes.author: Ayya Khema
quotes.source: All of Us, I: The Dhamma of the Blessed One is Perfectly Expounded

quotes.text: We are blessed with an inner wealth.
quotes.author: Ayya Khema
quotes.source: All of Us, I: The Dhamma of the Blessed One is Perfectly Expounded

quotes.text: This is why people who are intelligent and discerning prefer criticism to praise. Stupid people prefer praise to criticism.
quotes.author: Upasika Kee Nanayon
quotes.source: Stop, Look, and Let Go, talk of 28 July 1965, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: It is by recognizing and honoring someone or something higher that one honors and enhances one's own inner potentialities.
quotes.author: Nyanaponika Thera
quotes.source: Devotion in Buddhism, discussion of respect and reverence

quotes.text: Washing my feet, I noticed the water.
quotes.author: Paṭācārā
quotes.source: Therīgāthā 5.10 (vv. 112–116), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Like the flame's unbinding was the liberation of awareness.
quotes.author: Paṭācārā
quotes.source: Therīgāthā 5.10 (vv. 112–116), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Associating with an admirable friend even a fool becomes wise.
quotes.author: Kisāgotamī
quotes.source: Therīgāthā 10.1 (vv. 213–223), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: I've cut out the arrow, put down the burden, done the task.
quotes.author: Kisāgotamī
quotes.source: Therīgāthā 10.1 (vv. 213–223), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Seeing the world's deep misery, we both went forth
quotes.author: Bhaddā Kāpilānī
quotes.source: Therīgāthā 4.1 (vv. 63–66), trans. Hellmuth Hecker and Sister Khema

quotes.text: Cooled of passions, we have found our freedom.
quotes.author: Bhaddā Kāpilānī
quotes.source: Therīgāthā 4.1 (vv. 63–66), trans. Hellmuth Hecker and Sister Khema

quotes.text: All ties — human & divine — have been cut.
quotes.author: Vimalā
quotes.source: Therīgāthā 5.2 (vv. 72–76), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Having cast off all effluents, cooled am I, unbound.
quotes.author: Vimalā
quotes.source: Therīgāthā 5.2 (vv. 72–76), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: The five aggregates, comprehended, stand like a tree with its root cut through.
quotes.author: Soṇā
quotes.source: Therīgāthā 5.8 (vv. 102–106), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: I develop the theme-less meditation, well-focused oneness.
quotes.author: Soṇā
quotes.source: Therīgāthā 5.8 (vv. 102–106), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: They do the best work: They abandon passion & anger.
quotes.author: Rohiṇī
quotes.source: Therīgāthā 13.2 (vv. 271–290), Rohiṇī's speech, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Take on the precepts: That will lead to your well-being.
quotes.author: Rohiṇī
quotes.source: Therīgāthā 13.2 (vv. 271–290), Rohiṇī's speech, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Let the robe be yours. I don't need it.
quotes.author: Puṇṇikā
quotes.source: Therīgāthā 12.1 (vv. 236–251), Puṇṇikā's speech, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Take on the precepts: That will lead to your liberation.
quotes.author: Puṇṇikā
quotes.source: Therīgāthā 12.1 (vv. 236–251), Puṇṇikā's speech, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: You make things worse when you flare up at someone who's angry.
quotes.author: Brahmadatta
quotes.source: Theragāthā 6.12 (vv. 441–446), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Don't let the moment pass you by.
quotes.author: Revata
quotes.source: Theragāthā 14.1 (vv. 645–658), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Attain completion through heedfulness: that is my message.
quotes.author: Revata
quotes.source: Theragāthā 14.1 (vv. 645–658), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: … those who are filled with discernment — as the ocean, with water — don't look down on others.
quotes.author: Godatta
quotes.source: Theragāthā 14.2 (vv. 659–672), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: For them there is nothing dear or undear.
quotes.author: Godatta
quotes.source: Theragāthā 14.2 (vv. 659–672), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: The Dhamma protects those who live by the Dhamma.
quotes.author: Dhammika
quotes.source: Theragāthā 4.10 (vv. 303–306), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: The Dhamma well-practiced brings bliss.
quotes.author: Dhammika
quotes.source: Theragāthā 4.10 (vv. 303–306), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Their lovely surfaces wet with rain, mountains frequented by seers & echoing with peacocks: those rocky crags refresh me.
quotes.author: Mahā Kassapa
quotes.source: Theragāthā 18 (vv. 1051–1090), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: I myself will bring it about. No one can do it for anyone else.
quotes.author: Ekavihāriya
quotes.source: Theragāthā 10.2 (vv. 537–546), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: As I desire to do this, may my purpose succeed.
quotes.author: Ekavihāriya
quotes.source: Theragāthā 10.2 (vv. 537–546), trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Be steadfast in your effort.
quotes.author: Webu Sayadaw
quotes.source: The Essential Practice: Part I, What Really Matters, trans. Roger Bischoff (Wheel Nos. 375–376)

quotes.text: Strive with happiness in your heart and when you are successful, be truly happy.
quotes.author: Webu Sayadaw
quotes.source: The Essential Practice: Part I, What Really Matters, trans. Roger Bischoff (Wheel Nos. 375–376)

quotes.text: The Buddha declares that he teaches the Dhamma for the sole purpose of leading beings to freedom from suffering.
quotes.author: Nyanaponika Thera
quotes.source: Why End Suffering?, opening paragraph

quotes.text: Regarded from another angle, giving can also be identified with the personal quality of generosity (caga).
quotes.author: Bhikkhu Bodhi
quotes.source: Dana: The Practice of Giving, Introduction (Wheel Nos. 367–369)

quotes.text: To heal the wounds of our world we must work to heal the wounds of our heart, the deep hidden wounds of greed, hatred, and delusion.
quotes.author: Bhikkhu Bodhi
quotes.source: Facing the Future: Four Essays on Buddhism and Society (Wheel 438/440), p. 33

quotes.text: What we must do is replace greed with non-greed: with generosity, detachment, contentment, and simplicity.
quotes.author: Bhikkhu Bodhi
quotes.source: Facing the Future: Four Essays on Buddhism and Society (Wheel 438/440), p. 28

quotes.text: Craving is blind desire, a self-centred drive for sensual pleasure, power, and status.
quotes.author: Bhikkhu Bodhi
quotes.source: Facing the Future: Four Essays on Buddhism and Society (Wheel 438/440), p. 24

quotes.text: The realization that happiness cannot be bought in the shopping mall should awaken in us an urgent desire to find a more genuine sense of meaning for our lives, a peace and happiness that does not depend on outer conditions.
quotes.author: Bhikkhu Bodhi
quotes.source: Facing the Future: Four Essays on Buddhism and Society (Wheel 438/440), p. 68

quotes.text: Instead of hoarding and accumulating things, Buddhism emphasizes the value of giving: the practice of generosity is the most effective way to erase the greed from one’s own mind as well as to confer benefits on others.
quotes.author: Bhikkhu Bodhi
quotes.source: Facing the Future: Four Essays on Buddhism and Society (Wheel 438/440), p. 28

quotes.text: We conquer ourselves, we don't try to conquer others.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Food for the Heart, Dhamma Fighting; Sangha translation
quotes.comment: Additional Thai Forest teachings verified 2 October 2026.

quotes.text: Practice of the Dhamma is not done by following your moods.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Food for the Heart, Dhamma Fighting; Sangha translation

quotes.text: The true refuge is the trained mind.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Bodhinyana, Fragments of a Teaching; trans. Sangha, Bung Wai Forest Monastery

quotes.text: Teachers are those who only point out the direction of the Path.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Bodhinyana, Fragments of a Teaching; trans. Sangha, Bung Wai Forest Monastery

quotes.text: We have to come back to ourselves.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Living Dhamma, Why are we here?; trans. Sangha, Wat Pah Nanachat

quotes.text: If we don't have wisdom everything round us will be a source of suffering.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Living Dhamma, Why are we here?; trans. Sangha, Wat Pah Nanachat

quotes.text: To calm the mind means to find the right balance.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Taste of Freedom, On Meditation; trans. Ajahn Puriso

quotes.text: When we see the truth, peace arises.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Taste of Freedom, On Meditation; trans. Ajahn Puriso

quotes.text: Even peace must be seen as impermanent. If you are attached to peaceful states of mind you will suffer when you do not have them.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Bodhinyana, "Questions and Answers"; trans. Sangha, Bung Wai Forest Monastery

quotes.text: Actually, this suffering is what brings us wisdom; it makes us contemplate dukkha. Happiness (sukha) tends to make us close our eyes and ears. It never allows us to develop patience.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Bodhinyana, "The Training of the Heart"; trans. Sangha, Bung Wai Forest Monastery

quotes.text: Don’t hold that one only meditates while sitting or walking. Everything and everywhere is our practice.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Bodhinyana, "The Training of the Heart"; trans. Sangha, Bung Wai Forest Monastery

quotes.text: The practice is not to try to achieve anything. Just be mindful of what is. Our whole meditation is looking directly at the mind.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Bodhinyana, "Questions and Answers"; trans. Sangha, Bung Wai Forest Monastery

quotes.text: When anger arises, it grows and changes and finally disappears. Happiness, too, arises, grows and changes and finally disappears. They are empty.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Bodhinyana, "Dhamma Nature"; trans. Sangha, Bung Wai Forest Monastery

quotes.text: Be patient. Patience and endurance are necessary. If you act naturally and are mindful, wisdom will come naturally too.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Bodhinyana, "Questions and Answers"; trans. Sangha, Bung Wai Forest Monastery

quotes.text: Knowing is fifty percent even if we are unable to let go. Though we can’t let go, we do understand that letting go of these things will bring peace.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Everything Is Teaching Us, "Right Restraint" (Amaravati Publications, 2018)

quotes.text: We want to be teaching the mind, not merely controlling it, so that it becomes aware. Too much forcing will make you crazy.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Everything Is Teaching Us, "Knowing the World" (Amaravati Publications, 2018)

quotes.text: Put love to one side, hate to the other side. Put happiness to one side, suffering to the other side. Remain in the middle without letting the mind go in either direction.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Everything Is Teaching Us, "About Being Careful" (Amaravati Publications, 2018)

quotes.text: If we let the water in the basin settle and become still, we can see all sorts of things reflected in it. When the mind is settled and still, wisdom will be able to see things.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Everything Is Teaching Us, "Wholehearted Training" (Amaravati Publications, 2018)

quotes.text: Some people get the idea that any kind of desire, such as desire for food and the material requisites for life, is taṇhā. But we can have this kind of desire in an ordinary and natural way.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Everything Is Teaching Us, "About Being Careful" (Amaravati Publications, 2018)

quotes.text: Getting beyond suffering does not depend on others’ opinions of us, but on our own individual state of mind.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: Everything Is Teaching Us, "Wholehearted Training" (Amaravati Publications, 2018)

quotes.text: Samadhi is one kind of peace, like the stone covering the grass. This is only a temporary peace. The peace of wisdom is like putting the stone down and just leaving it there.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Tree in a Forest: A Collection of Ajahn Chah's Similes, "Grass", p. 39

quotes.text: Read yourself, not books. Truth isn’t outside. That’s only memory, not wisdom. Memory without wisdom is like an empty thermos bottle — if you don’t fill it, it’s useless.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Tree in a Forest: A Collection of Ajahn Chah's Similes, "Thermos Bottle", p. 59

quotes.text: If you clearly see the truth through meditation, then suffering will become unwound, just like a screw.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Tree in a Forest: A Collection of Ajahn Chah's Similes, "Screw", p. 55

quotes.text: You don’t have to read the Tipitaka to have greed, hatred and delusion. They are all already in your mind, and you don’t have to study books to have them.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Tree in a Forest: A Collection of Ajahn Chah's Similes, "Grand Central Station", p. 85

quotes.text: In truth, happiness is suffering in disguise, but in such a subtle form that you don’t see it.
quotes.author: Ajahn Chah
quotes.source: A Tree in a Forest: A Collection of Ajahn Chah's Similes, "Piece of Cake", p. 103

quotes.text: Even our enemies, when we become familiar with them, can become our friends.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: The Demons of Defilement, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: An excellent person takes something good and makes it better.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: The Demons of Defilement, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: If you have effort but no endurance, you won't get anywhere.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Consciousnesses, opening teaching on persistence; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: So we should regard effort as coming first, and endurance second.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Consciousnesses, opening teaching on persistence; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Whoever trains the mind to be centered gains a refuge.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Keeping the Breath in Mind, Introduction; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: A centered mind is like a fortress.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Keeping the Breath in Mind, Introduction; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: So you have to be observant.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Knowledge, discussion of directed thought and evaluation; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: If you think too much, it'll run away with your concentration.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Knowledge, discussion of directed thought and evaluation; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Clinging is the cause of all suffering and stress.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Starting Out Small, Clinging; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Thoughts of past and future are things we don't need to think about.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Starting Out Small, Clinging; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Keep practicing concentration until your heart matures, step by step.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Food for Thought, An Inner Mainstay and Bodily Debts; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: All the attachment comes from our side alone.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Food for Thought, An Inner Mainstay and Bodily Debts; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: If the mind is murky, make it clear.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Inner Strength, A Mind of Pure Gold; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Set your heart on doing it right now.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Inner Strength, A Mind of Pure Gold; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Don't forget the people who have helped you.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: The Skill of Release, The Affairs of the World; compiled and trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Find some way of doing good to repay them.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: The Skill of Release, The Affairs of the World; compiled and trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Don't latch onto what you see, because all things are inconstant.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Starting Out Small (Portfolio 2), Coming Ashore; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: There's nothing certain or dependable at all.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Starting Out Small (Portfolio 2), Coming Ashore; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: When you think, you do it with a mind of good will.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Starting Out Small (Portfolio 3), The Essence of Merit; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: When you speak, you do it with a mind of good will.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: Starting Out Small (Portfolio 3), The Essence of Merit; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Regard what you've done as your wealth.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: The Power of Goodness, 4 October 1960; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: So you shouldn't underestimate the power of goodness.
quotes.author: Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo
quotes.source: The Power of Goodness, 4 October 1960; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Don't let your attention stray out ahead or behind.
quotes.author: Ajahn Tate
quotes.source: Buddho, meditation instructions; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Let things follow their own course.
quotes.author: Ajahn Tate
quotes.source: Buddho, meditation instructions; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Don't let feelings of greed or desire, disappointment or dejection arise.
quotes.author: Ajahn Tate
quotes.source: Steps Along the Path, meditation instructions; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Let there simply be awareness and the act of focusing.
quotes.author: Ajahn Tate
quotes.source: Steps Along the Path, meditation instructions; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: It is the present moment that is important.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sim Buddhacaro
quotes.source: Simply So, Source and Stream; trans. Jayasaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Be vigilant and care for the mind right here.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sim Buddhacaro
quotes.source: Simply So, Source and Stream; trans. Jayasaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Practice is what keeps the true Dhamma pure.
quotes.author: Ajahn Mun Bhuridatta
quotes.source: A Heart Released, §§1–2 section headings; recorded teachings, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: To follow the Buddha, we must train ourselves well before training others.
quotes.author: Ajahn Mun Bhuridatta
quotes.source: A Heart Released, §§1–2 section headings; recorded teachings, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: To listen well, your heart has to be quiet and still.
quotes.author: Ajahn Fuang
quotes.source: Awareness Itself, People Practicing the Dhamma; compiled and trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: You listen with your heart, not just with your ears.
quotes.author: Ajahn Fuang
quotes.source: Awareness Itself, People Practicing the Dhamma; compiled and trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Suffering is something to be comprehended.
quotes.author: Ajahn Dune Atulo
quotes.source: Gifts He Left Behind, §24, Throw it away; compiled by Phra Bodhinandamuni, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: When you comprehend it, you let it go.
quotes.author: Ajahn Dune Atulo
quotes.source: Gifts He Left Behind, §24, Throw it away; compiled by Phra Bodhinandamuni, trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: If we want to study the Dhamma, we have to study our own heart.
quotes.author: Ajahn Suwat Suvaco
quotes.source: A Fistful of Sand, A Fistful of Sand; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: Simply be mindful of the breath.
quotes.author: Ajahn Suwat Suvaco
quotes.source: A Fistful of Sand, A Fistful of Sand; trans. Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: The important factor in any method of mind-development is mindfulness (Sati).
quotes.author: Ajahn Maha Bua
quotes.source: The Dhamma Teaching of Acariya Maha Boowa in London, opening meditation instructions; trans. Bhikkhu Paññavaddho

quotes.text: Forgetting mindfulness means failing in one's task, and one will not get results.
quotes.author: Ajahn Maha Bua
quotes.source: The Dhamma Teaching of Acariya Maha Boowa in London, opening meditation instructions; trans. Bhikkhu Paññavaddho

quotes.text: What knows the pain isn’t the pain. It’s the heart. The heart is what knows all about the pain.
quotes.author: Ajahn Maha Bua
quotes.source: Samaṇa, "Right Here in the Heart", adapted from translations by Thanissaro Bhikkhu (Forest Dhamma Books, 2011)

quotes.text: When the mind doesn’t get itself worked up with thoughts about various things, it becomes still; that’s all there is to it.
quotes.author: Ajahn Maha Bua
quotes.source: Samaṇa, "Right Here in the Heart", adapted from translations by Thanissaro Bhikkhu (Forest Dhamma Books, 2011)

quotes.text: Once the mind knows, it is bound to let go of its own accord. The clinging mind is the mind that doesn’t yet know, doesn’t yet understand with wisdom.
quotes.author: Ajahn Maha Bua
quotes.source: Samaṇa, "Birth and Death", adapted from translations by Thanissaro Bhikkhu (Forest Dhamma Books, 2011)

quotes.text: When we enjoy the beginning but dislike the end – when we like birth but dislike death – we’re contradicting the truth all the time.
quotes.author: Ajahn Maha Bua
quotes.source: Samaṇa, "Right Here in the Heart", adapted from translations by Thanissaro Bhikkhu (Forest Dhamma Books, 2011)

quotes.text: When mindfulness loses its focus, the defilements rush in to drag your thoughts to a past long gone, or a future yet to come.
quotes.author: Ajahn Maha Bua
quotes.source: Samaṇa, "The Heart of a Samaṇa", adapted from translations by Thanissaro Bhikkhu (Forest Dhamma Books, 2011)

quotes.text: Mindfulness fixes the mind in the present, allowing wisdom to focus sharply. Learned experience is stored as memory, and as such should be put aside; otherwise memory will masquerade as wisdom.
quotes.author: Ajahn Maha Bua
quotes.source: Arahattamagga – Arahattaphala, Part 1, trans. Bhikkhu Dick Sīlaratano (Forest Dhamma Books, 2005)

quotes.text: The same body that was there when the pain appeared is still there when the pain ceases. Pain does not alter the nature of the body; the body does not affect the nature of pain.
quotes.author: Ajahn Maha Bua
quotes.source: Arahattamagga – Arahattaphala, Part 1, trans. Bhikkhu Dick Sīlaratano (Forest Dhamma Books, 2005)

quotes.text: In truth, the mind paints elaborate pictures all the time—pictures of oneself and pictures of the external world. It then falls for its own mental imagery, believing it to be real.
quotes.author: Ajahn Maha Bua
quotes.source: Arahattamagga – Arahattaphala, Part 1, trans. Bhikkhu Dick Sīlaratano (Forest Dhamma Books, 2005)

quotes.text: One accepts death—when it comes—as well as life—when it continues. Both are aspects of the same truth.
quotes.author: Ajahn Maha Bua
quotes.source: Arahattamagga – Arahattaphala, Part 1, trans. Bhikkhu Dick Sīlaratano (Forest Dhamma Books, 2005)

quotes.text: Unless it supports the development of wisdom, samādhi can sidetrack a meditator from the path to the end of all suffering.
quotes.author: Ajahn Maha Bua
quotes.source: Arahattamagga – Arahattaphala, Part 1, trans. Bhikkhu Dick Sīlaratano (Forest Dhamma Books, 2005)

quotes.text: The thinking mind is fabricated; the knowing mind is genuine. The thinking mind is intellect, defiled and complicated, whereas the knowing mind is awareness itself—pure and simple.
quotes.author: Ajahn Jia Cundo
quotes.source: Gold Wrapped in Rags: Autobiography of Ajaan Jia Cundo, "Bones", trans. Ajaan Dick Sīlaratano (Forest Dhamma Publications, 2024)

quotes.text: How much we suffer from painful feelings depends more on the degree to which we cling to our bodies than it does on the severity of the affliction the body endures.
quotes.author: Ajahn Jia Cundo
quotes.source: Gold Wrapped in Rags: Autobiography of Ajaan Jia Cundo, "Wilds", trans. Ajaan Dick Sīlaratano (Forest Dhamma Publications, 2024)

quotes.text: Unsupported by Dhamma and left to its own desires, the heart will be unable to experience genuine happiness, even with a mountain of valuable possessions at its disposal.
quotes.author: Ajahn Jia Cundo
quotes.source: Gold Wrapped in Rags: Autobiography of Ajaan Jia Cundo, "Caves", trans. Ajaan Dick Sīlaratano (Forest Dhamma Publications, 2024)

quotes.text: Merit encompasses all the good and noble intentions in the mind. That’s where inner worth resides.
quotes.author: Ajahn Jia Cundo
quotes.source: Gold Wrapped in Rags: Autobiography of Ajaan Jia Cundo, "Seeds", trans. Ajaan Dick Sīlaratano (Forest Dhamma Publications, 2024)

quotes.text: Everyone who is born must die—such is the nature of the world. It’s fruitless trying to resist that truth.
quotes.author: Ajahn Jia Cundo
quotes.source: Gold Wrapped in Rags: Autobiography of Ajaan Jia Cundo, "Wilds", trans. Ajaan Dick Sīlaratano (Forest Dhamma Publications, 2024)

quotes.text: We begin to notice the details of kindness and our world becomes much happier.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sundara
quotes.source: On the Way to Liberation, reflection of 20 September 2015, Amaravati Buddhist Monastery

quotes.text: And we need to make peace with our delusion.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sundara
quotes.source: On the Way to Liberation, reflection of 20 September 2015, Amaravati Buddhist Monastery

quotes.text: The world is the suffering we create. The Buddha says this world is in this fathom-long body – that is where the world arises and ends.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sundara
quotes.source: Walking the World, p. 52

quotes.text: Everything in life influences us, and awareness is key. Awareness of mistakes can take us right into the fire. Sometimes not getting it quite right is what wakes you up much more sharply than developing a lot of techniques for being aware.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sundara
quotes.source: Walking the World, "It Can Be Very Simple", p. 61

quotes.text: When you have seen with insight that the things we crave are not really worth making ourselves miserable for, it becomes possible to be at peace with whatever is happening.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sundara
quotes.source: Walking the World, p. 62

quotes.text: Practice is a selfless act. We practise not to gain anything, not to realize our dreams, but just to practise.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sundara
quotes.source: Walking the World, "Mindfulness and Wisdom: The Tools of Practice", p. 75

quotes.text: If we ask ourselves honestly, we might find that actually we like our conflict, chaos and delusion, that in many ways we find them quite exciting!
quotes.author: Ajahn Sundara
quotes.source: Walking the World, "Our Nature", p. 89

quotes.text: Delusion, the Buddha teaches, is not a curse. It’s part of nature. He tells us that by seeing it and understanding its cause, we can liberate ourselves from it.
quotes.author: Ajahn Sundara
quotes.source: Walking the World, "Our Nature", p. 89

quotes.text: We make peace with things just as they are.
quotes.author: Ajahn Candasiri
quotes.source: Simple Kindness, The Four Noble Truths, p. 16 (2012)

quotes.text: In that way a real transformation can happen.
quotes.author: Ajahn Candasiri
quotes.source: Simple Kindness, The Four Noble Truths, p. 18, on self-forgiveness (2012)

quotes.text: The reasons to practice, are superior to the excuses not to.
quotes.author: Ajahn Achalo
quotes.source: What I teach intermediate and advanced, Talk 2026-10-13, Anandagiri Forest Monastery
